security-guidance hook broken with whitespace in plugin root
hook command unquoted path expansion fails
signals.review_reason: Edits to security-guidance are a core workflow step. Hook silently fails on every Edit/Write/MultiEdit for affected users (common on Windows with spaces in username or Program Files). Two independent reporters provide concrete error traces and reproduction steps. Though count=2, the impact is high (every edit call fails) and the user base affected is large given how common spaces are in Windows paths. Downgraded from P0 to P1 per rule that count<3 without overwhelming evidence.

source_issues.title: security-guidance: PreToolUse hook fails on Windows when ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} expands to a path containing spaces
source_issues.evidence: On Windows with space in username (e.g. 'Catalin Teodorescu'), every Edit/Write/MultiEdit call fails silently. Python receives truncated path and throws "can't find '__main__' module". Verified fix with args[] form.

source_issues.title: Unquoted ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in security-guidance hook command breaks when path contains a space
source_issues.evidence: On macOS with HOME under 'Application Support' path containing spaces, Edit/Write fails with "can't open file ... 'Library/Application': [Errno 2] No such file or directory". Shell word-splits the unquoted variable expansion.

signals.topic: Telegram bot .env loader silently skips TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN when file has UTF-8 BOM
signals.summary: Telegram plugin's .env parser fails to read the bot token when the file was written by Windows PowerShell with UTF-8 BOM encoding, causing the MCP server to exit at startup without clear diagnostic.
aliases: telegram bot token not loaded with BOM
telegram .env loader BOM issue windows powershell
signals.review_reason: Blocks the Telegram bot from starting on Windows when .env is written through standard Windows tooling. User sees silent failure — bot doesn't reply, configure skill misleadingly says 'token set'. Confirmed reproducible on Windows 11 Pro with PowerShell. count=1 but single-instance impact is complete plugin unavailability on affected platform.

source_issues.title: [telegram] .env loader skips TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN line when file has UTF-8 BOM
source_issues.evidence: Windows PowerShell Out-File/Set-Content writes UTF-8 BOM (EF BB BF). Parser regex ^(\w+) fails on BOM prefix, token line is silently skipped, server exits with 'TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN required' even though value is present. configure skill reports 'token set' masking the failure. Confirmed on Windows 11 Pro.

signals.topic: Telegram orphaned bun processes peg CPU at 100% and ignore SIGTERM after session crash
signals.summary: Telegram MCP server bun processes survive parent session crash, become orphans adopted by launchd, enter busy loop at 100% CPU indefinitely, and cannot be killed by SIGTERM (only SIGKILL works).
aliases: telegram bun orphan process SIGTERM ignore
telegram bun busy loop after session crash
signals.review_reason: Sustained 100% CPU per orphan with real battery drain (30-40W on Apple Silicon). Processes ignore SIGTERM and only die via SIGKILL. Existing PID-file cleanup only runs at next session start, not proactively. Clear cost/resource impact per the pain point definition.

source_issues.title: telegram plugin v0.0.6: orphaned bun server.ts processes peg CPU 100%, ignore SIGTERM, accumulate indefinitely
source_issues.evidence: Orphaned bun processes confirmed at 99.9% CPU for 14 days on macOS. SIGTERM ignored by stuck bun. Accumulate over weeks, causing 200% CPU total and 30-40W battery drain on Apple Silicon. Workaround requires SIGKILL only. Existing SIGTERM-only PID cleanup is insufficient.

signals.topic: Telegram poller silently dies after claude mcp list or /mcp health check from another session
signals.summary: Running claude mcp list or /mcp from any session spawns a transient poller that SIGTERMs the long-running session's poller, then exits. Incoming Telegram DMs stop being delivered with no error shown.
aliases: telegram poller stolen by health check
telegram incoming messages stop after mcp list
telegram long polling dies after transient invocation
signals.review_reason: The Telegram bot becomes read-only (incoming DMs silently stop) after any health check, which is a common operation. The session reports 'Connected' masking the broken state. Outgoing replies still work but the user cannot receive messages. Multi-editor/multi-session workflows (common with Cursor + terminal setups) trigger this frequently.

source_issues.title: Telegram channel poller silently dies after claude mcp list or /mcp health check from another session
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced: start long-running session, confirm Telegram DMs work, run 'claude mcp list', new DMs are not delivered. claude mcp list reports 'Connected' because it spawns its own poller, masking the broken state. Log shows churn of 'replacing stale poller' from each transient invocation.

signals.topic: setup.sh script fails on Windows due to incorrect virtual environment activation path
signals.summary: The setup.sh script hardcodes `.venv/bin/activate` which only works on Linux/macOS, causing the script to fail on Windows with 'No such file or directory' error
signals.review_reason: Windows users cannot complete the quickstart setup workflow — the setup.sh script fails at the virtual environment activation step with a clear error, completely blocking onboarding for Windows users. Even though count=1 and single-repo, the issue is labeled 'bug' with 'windows' tag and has active engagement, and the user impact is unambiguous (script exits with error before setup completes).

source_issues.title: Inconsistent Virtual Environment Activation Path for Windows in `setup.sh` Script
source_issues.evidence: Script fails with 'No such file or directory' when running `./setup.sh` on Windows, blocking the entire quickstart setup workflow for Windows users

signals.topic: Broken README link to browser-tools-api-demo causes demo page to be unresolvable
signals.summary: README contains a link to the browser-tools-api-demo that returns HTTP 404, preventing users from accessing the demo
signals.review_reason: Users clicking the README link to the browser-tools-api-demo receive a 404 error and cannot access the demo content. This is a clear UX degradation where a documented resource is completely inaccessible. While not a runtime block, it prevents users from completing a key learning path referenced in the documentation.

source_issues.title: Documentation: Broken link in README
source_issues.evidence: README link to browser-tools-api-demo returns HTTP 404, user screenshot shows '404 - page not found' error

signals.topic: No native mechanism to share or sync skills across team members or machines
signals.summary: ~/.claude/skills/ is per-machine with no built-in sync. Teams adopting skills at scale must resort to fragile workarounds: git submodules (breaks onboarding), dotfiles-style sync (drifts over time), or custom self-hosted registries. Additionally, there is no org-level skill sharing in Claude.ai — users must download, manually transfer, and re-upload skills. Both the local sync and org-level sharing gaps create significant friction for multi-engineer teams.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports (from different authors, different dates) both describing the same root problem: no native team/machine skill sharing mechanism. This is not a bug per se but a significant adoption blocker for teams. Issue 1132 describes per-machine friction with 5 engineers; issue 228 describes org-level sharing gap with 13 commenters confirming demand. Both represent real workflow friction causing manual workarounds.

source_issues.title: docs: any guidance on sharing SKILL.md across a team?
source_issues.evidence: User at ~5-engineer team hit friction immediately. ~.claude/skills/ is per-machine — adding a new skill means everyone re-syncs manually. Three workarounds attempted (git submodule, dotfiles sync, self-hosted registry).

source_issues.title: Enable org-wide skill sharing in Claude.ai
source_issues.evidence: Users must download .skill file, send via Slack/Teams, and manually navigate Settings > Capabilities to upload — 13 comments indicating widespread demand for org-level sharing. Blocking adoption at organizational scale.

signals.topic: xlsx skill crashes on Windows Python builds due to unguarded AF_UNIX socket access
signals.summary: recalc.py calls _needs_shim() which accesses socket.AF_UNIX without an hasattr guard. On Windows Python builds where AF_UNIX is unavailable as an attribute, this raises AttributeError — uncaught by the surrounding try/except OSError — crashing the entire xlsx skill before any LibreOffice work begins. Users must fall back to manual soffice commands as a workaround.
signals.review_reason: This is a complete workflow-blocking bug. recalc.py is a core component of the xlsx skill — it crashes on startup on any Windows Python build where AF_UNIX is absent, making the entire skill inoperable for that platform. Full reproduction trace and root cause analysis are provided. While count=1, the impact is absolute (skill broken, not degraded), and the fix is two lines of hasattr guard — a clear defect, not an edge case.

source_issues.title: xlsx recalc.py crashes on Windows: unguarded socket.AF_UNIX access
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace provided; AttributeError: module 'socket' has no attribute 'AF_UNIX' on Windows 11 + Python 3.14.4 (uv-managed cpython-3.14-windows-x86_64-none). _needs_shim() only catches OSError, not AttributeError. Skill completely unusable on affected environments.

signals.topic: run_eval.py evaluation framework has 0% skill trigger rate, making the eval tool unreliable
signals.summary: run_eval.py places skill definitions in .claude/commands/ and runs claude -p, but claude -p never triggers skills/commands — every should-trigger query scores 0/3 across all evaluated skills (144 queries across 8 skills). Even an explicit 'run /skill-name please' fails to trigger. The entire eval framework is unreliable for measuring skill invocation accuracy.
signals.review_reason: This is a primary-flow failure of a core tool. run_eval.py is the evaluation harness for the entire skills ecosystem — a 0% trigger rate means the eval tool cannot measure whether skills fire correctly at all. This undermines the fundamental reliability of the skill ecosystem. count=1 but with 8+ comments confirming the issue is real and ongoing.

source_issues.title: run_eval.py: claude -p never triggers skills/commands (0% trigger rate across all queries)
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced with 8 different skills, 144 total queries, 0/3 trigger rate for every should-trigger case. Explicit invocation ('run /lucas:memory-layer please') also 0/3. 8 comments indicating ongoing discussion. Affects the entire eval framework reliability.

signals.topic: node -e inline execution corrupts CJK/multi-byte UTF-8 content in docx generation
signals.summary: The docx skill defaults to node -e for inline script execution. When scripts contain Chinese, Japanese, or Korean characters, the shell processes the argument string and mangles multi-byte UTF-8 sequences before Node sees them, resulting in garbled or ?-substituted CJK characters in the output .docx file. The model eventually self-corrects by switching to file-based execution but wastes multiple token rounds in the process.
signals.review_reason: This causes output quality degradation and direct cost loss (wasted token rounds) for CJK users of the docx skill. While self-correcting, the failure is predictable and avoidable with minimal guidance. Count=1 but impact is clear and reproducible — shell-level UTF-8 mangling is deterministic for multi-byte characters.

source_issues.title: node -e inline execution tends to corrupt CJK / non-ASCII content
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified: shell processes the string argument and corrupts multi-byte sequences before Node sees them. Self-correction does eventually happen but wastes token rounds. Proposed fix with heredoc workaround documented. Impact is output quality degradation and wasted cost for any user generating docx files with CJK content.

signals.topic: known_location() regression — all Gemini 3.x models broken, API calls return 404 silently
signals.summary: The `known_location()` function returns 'Iowa' for all Gemini model variants, but Gemini 3.x models require the global API endpoint. Requests are silently routed to `us-central1` and return 404 with no retry, breaking all Gemini 3.x usage.
signals.review_reason: 关键模型服务中断回归：Gemini 3.x 在默认配置下完全不可用，API 调用静默 404 无重试。虽然已 closed（修复中），但存在真实用户影响证据，属于明显服务降级。count=2 有两份独立报告支撑。

source_issues.title: Regression: known_location() returns Iowa for all Gemini models, breaking Gemini 3.x (global-endpoint only)
source_issues.evidence: 关键模型全线故障：known_location() 硬编码返回 Iowa，导致所有 Gemini 3.x 模型请求 404 无响应。降级重试机制依赖 configured_location != known_location()，默认配置下不触发，用户无任何错误提示。

source_issues.title: Regression: known_location() returns Iowa for all Gemini models, breaking Gemini 3.x (global-endpoint only)
source_issues.evidence: 同 #9141 的重复报告，同一回归问题。

signals.topic: Windows OAuth authentication completely blocked — browser fails to launch in corporate environments
signals.summary: On Windows corporate environments, Goose cannot launch a browser for OAuth authentication (GitHub Copilot, Azure AD), blocking the core authentication flow entirely. Executables like `az` and Edge are missing from system PATH, and there is no way to configure custom paths.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：OAuth 认证是 Goose 桌面端的核心功能，用户在 Windows 企业环境（PATH 中无可用浏览器执行文件）下完全无法完成认证，属于 P0 级别阻断性 bug。

source_issues.title: Windows: Browser not launching for authentication
source_issues.evidence: OAuth auth flow is completely blocked on Windows corporate machines — no browser window opens, users cannot authenticate with GitHub Copilot or Azure AD. Executables (az, Edge) are not in PATH and no config workaround exists.

signals.topic: Docker memory leak when MCP tool returns very large responses (~3M characters)
signals.summary: When `goosed` runs in Docker and MCP tools return ~3 million character responses, memory usage spikes sharply and never decreases after the tool call finishes. The same workload on native macOS/Windows does not exhibit this behavior — memory returns to normal.
signals.review_reason: 高影响资源泄漏：Docker 环境下大响应导致内存永不释放，持续增长直至 OOM。对使用 Docker 部署的用户是阻断性问题，且在原生平台不存在，证明是 Docker 特定回归。

source_issues.title: Severe memory leak in Docker container when MCP tool returns very large responses (~3 million characters)
source_issues.evidence: 内存持续泄漏：Docker 环境中 MCP 工具返回约 300 万字符响应后，内存急剧飙升且不再回落。原生 macOS/Windows 不存在此问题，Docker 用户面临内存无限增长直至 OOM 的风险。

signals.topic: Session silently hangs after chat-mode response — subsequent messages accepted but never processed
signals.summary: After an agentic session enters chat mode and the LLM returns a text-only response (no tool_calls), the session stalls silently. Subsequent user messages are accepted and persisted to the DB, but no LLM call is fired. No error is shown to the user. The session appears active but is dead.
aliases: conversation dead after LLM text reply
signals.review_reason: 主流程静默阻断：对话在 LLM 返回纯文本后完全挂死，用户消息被静默接受但永远无响应，且无错误提示。属于核心对话流程的严重回归，用户体验极差。

source_issues.title: Session silently hangs after chat-mode response — subsequent user messages receive no response
source_issues.evidence: 会话静默挂死：LLM 返回纯文本回复后（tool_calls: []），会话不再响应用户后续消息。消息被写入数据库但无 LLM 调用，无任何错误提示，用户无法继续对话。

signals.topic: MCP OAuth opens 3 duplicate login pages on Windows — auth flow repeats 3x
signals.summary: On Windows 11, when using MCP servers that require OAuth authentication, Goose opens 3 separate OAuth login windows with different client_ids and redirect_uris. The auth flow discovery, registration, and session-start steps each repeat 3 times.
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降：MCP OAuth 认证流程重复 3 次，用户被迫处理多个重复登录页面。虽然有明确日志证据，但 count=1 且仅 Windows 特定，定级 P1。

source_issues.title: MCP HTTP Server — Goose opens 3 OAuth login pages on Windows
source_issues.evidence: 认证流程重复3次：Windows 11 下 MCP OAuth 认证打开 3 个重复登录页面，debug 日志显示 discovery、registration、session-start 各执行 3 次，用户体验极差，认证流程无法正常完成。

signals.topic: Agent cache 不记录/回放自定义工具调用（custom tools），导致 replay 时表单填充等关键操作被跳过
signals.summary: Agent 缓存功能无法记录和回放自定义工具（custom_tool），导致在 replay 时跳过表单填写等自定义工具调用，使登录和表单填充场景 replay 失败。
aliases: agent cache skips custom tools during replay
signals.review_reason: 该 issue 描述了真实的功能缺陷：agent cache 的 replay 机制无法处理 custom_tool 类型，导致用户在 replay 时关键操作（表单填写凭证）被静默跳过。这是一个主流程阻断性问题（replay 功能是缓存的核心价值），且有用户提供了精确的根因定位（两处代码缺失处理）。虽然 count=1，但影响明确且非边缘，属于核心功能的阻断性缺陷，符合 P1 条件（影响明显但非高频）。

source_issues.title: Agent cache does not record or replay custom tool calls
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1558 提供完整复现场景、根因分析（v3CuaAgentHandler.ts 中 custom_tool case 未调用 recordAgentReplayStep；AgentCache.ts 中 executeAgentReplayStep 缺少 custom_tool 处理逻辑，默认跳过）和明确用户影响：表单填充凭证在 replay 时被跳过，登录 replay 失败。issue 处于 open 状态且最近活跃（last_comment_days: 2）。

signals.topic: Symlink path validation bug in sandbox dedicated tools causes tool failures and cascading performance degradation
signals.summary: Dedicated sandbox tools (read_file/ls/grep/glob) fail with Permission denied on symlinked repos due to asymmetric path validation (Path.resolve() resolves symlinks before allowlist check, while bash bypasses it via string substitution). Forces bash fallback, doubling turn count and triggering recursion limit hits and false loop-detection positives.
aliases: Symlink path validation causes dedicated tools to fail
Sandbox path validation asymmetry between tools and bash
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断（工具不可用）+ 明确量化证据（效率从100%降至53.3%，turn数翻倍）。虽仅1条issue，但issue内提供了跨任务对比数据，且明确关联其他issue的症状（false loop-detection）。根因清晰，修复后可显著改善工具可用性和任务完成率。

source_issues.title: fix: Asymmetric path validation in sandbox tools causes dedicated tools to fail on symlinked repos
source_issues.evidence: Experimental data: symlink path drops dedicated-tool efficiency from 100% to 53.3%, doubles total turns (28 vs 14), forces bash fallback. Explicitly linked to #2820 (Scaffolding Loop) and #2517 (false LoopDetectionMiddleware positives).

signals.topic: MCP filesystem path access denied intermittently in Docker sandbox, requiring service restart
signals.summary: In Docker sandbox mode, MCP filesystem server reports 'Access denied - path outside allowed directories' after normal usage. The error maps Docker virtual paths back to host paths, causing path validation to fail. Intermittent but persistent once triggered, requiring full service restart to recover.
aliases: MCP filesystem access denied in Docker sandbox
Docker sandbox MCP path validation failure
signals.review_reason: MCP filesystem工具不可用+需重启才能恢复，属于关键功能中断。虽为偶发但一旦触发则持续失效，直接阻断用户在沙箱内的文件系统操作能力。提供了完整堆栈证据。

source_issues.title: docker sandbox模式的MCP服务偶尔会出现：Access denied - path outside allowed directories
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace showing langchain_mcp_adapters raises ToolException: 'Access denied - path outside allowed directories'. Error maps /mnt/user-data/workspace/agent-mail-relay/src/comm/factory.rs to host path /home/ubuntu/deerflow/..., causing filesystem tools to be completely unusable after occurrence. Requires restart to recover.

signals.topic: make up/deploy.sh fails when system lacks python3 command
signals.summary: The deploy.sh script defaults to python3 for generating BETTER_AUTH_SECRET. On systems without python3 in PATH, make up fails immediately with exit code 49, blocking deployment entirely.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断（部署失败），错误明确（Makefile:179 recipe failed），在无python3环境中100%触发。提供了具体错误行号和退出码，证据充分。

source_issues.title: make up启动时在deploy.sh中当系统没有python3时报错
source_issues.evidence: Makefile:179: recipe for target 'up' failed. Error 49 triggered when BETTER_AUTH_SECRET generation via python3 command fails. Blocks entire deployment workflow.

signals.topic: Web UI freezes during model thinking process across multiple models
signals.summary: The web frontend freezes/hangs while the model is producing thinking output. Affects multiple models (Kimi k2.5, Glm5, deepseek v4) in Ultra mode across all thinking level settings. Some models recover after a delay, others leave the page unresponsive.
aliases: Frontend freezes during model thinking output
Page hangs during agent thinking process
signals.review_reason: 体验显著下降（UI卡死），跨多模型复现（3个不同模型），但非主流程完全阻断，部分模型可恢复。提供截图证据。count=1且为UI问题，默认P2。

source_issues.title: 在回答思考过程中，网页会卡死
source_issues.evidence: Tested across Kimi k2.5, Glm5, deepseek v4 in Ultra mode at low/medium/high thinking levels. Page becomes unresponsive during thinking output. Includes screenshot evidence. Multiple models affected, suggesting a frontend rendering or streaming issue.

signals.topic: Images generated in sandbox are not visible/previewable/downloadable in frontend
signals.summary: Images generated by the agent inside the sandbox (e.g., /mnt/user-data/outputs/guangxi_2026-02-11.png) cannot be displayed, previewed, or downloaded in the web UI. Users have no way to access sandbox-generated visual outputs.
aliases: Sandbox-generated images not accessible in frontend
Image output from sandbox not visible to users
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用（图片输出完全不可见），用户无法获取任何沙箱生成的视觉内容。明确具体场景和文件路径，证据充分。虽仅1条issue但影响明确，优先级P1。

source_issues.title: 对话过程中根据数据生成的图片不显示，怎么解决？
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly reports generated images in sandbox (/mnt/user-data/outputs/) cannot be displayed, previewed, or downloaded in the UI. Specific file path provided: /mnt/user-data/outputs/guangxi_2026-02-11.png.

signals.topic: LLM provider API errors block main workflow with no automatic recovery
signals.summary: Various provider/model combinations (AWS bedrock, Gemini, DeepSeek V4, Claude Code, OpenAI GPT-5 reasoning+tool_call) cause API errors that corrupt or block the current conversation, with no auto-recovery.
aliases: AWS bedrock region error on upgrade
DeepSeek V4 Pro tool call skip/hang
Claude Code provider command failed exit code 1
signals.review_reason: Five distinct provider/model combinations all fail with API-level errors that corrupt the session and prevent automatic recovery. This directly blocks the main workflow — users cannot complete tasks with AWS bedrock, Gemini, DeepSeek V4, OpenAI GPT-5, or Claude Code provider. The count=5 with each causing workflow blockage qualifies as P0.

source_issues.title: Error: AWS region setting is missing. Pass it using the 'region' parameter or the AWS_REGION environment variable.

source_issues.title: Getting an error with any Gemini model
source_issues.evidence: Gemini: 'GenerateContentRequest.contents[2].parts[0].function_response.name: Name cannot be empty' error on any Gemini model; complete workflow blocked.

source_issues.title: OpenAI-compatible DeepSeek V4 Pro/Flash stuck after command status becomes "Skipped"

source_issues.title: Latest Cline still hits OpenAI Native gpt-5.3-codex, gpt-5.4 and gpt-5.5 reasoning/function_call pairing error during MCP/tool use
source_issues.evidence: OpenAI gpt-5.3-codex to gpt-5.5: 400 error 'function_call was provided without its required reasoning item' during MCP/tool use; conversation corrupted; auto-retry does not recover; requires new task or context clear.

source_issues.title: Issue with Claude Code Provider
source_issues.evidence: Claude Code provider: valid subscription, but only runs a few steps then repeatedly fails with 'Command failed with exit code 1'. Works fine with direct Anthropic API key.

signals.topic: Command execution failure causes agent to permanently stuck in terminal state, requiring full IDE restart

Agent stuck at Skipped after DeepSeek tool call
Permanent Pending state blocks all further tasks

source_issues.title: Agent gets permanently stuck in "Pending" state after failed command execution, requires VS Code restart
source_issues.evidence: Command corrupted during transmission (git→it); agent enters permanent Pending state after failure; cannot cancel or recover; requires full VS Code restart. Auto-retry path never triggered.

source_issues.title: OpenAI-compatible DeepSeek V4 Pro/Flash stuck after command status becomes "Skipped"
source_issues.evidence: DeepSeek V4 Pro/Flash: command sometimes becomes 'skip'; extension completely stuck; cannot start new task, send new message, or resume after clicking cancel.

signals.topic: Context auto-compacts silently despite user disabling the setting, causing agent to forget task history and redo work
signals.summary: Cline silently runs context compaction even when the autocompacting setting is explicitly disabled, causing the context bar to run backwards, agent to forget important information, and users to lose progress.
signals.review_reason: User explicitly disabled auto-compaction but Cline silently ignores the setting and compacts anyway, causing measurable context loss (bar runs backwards) and forcing the agent to redo already completed work. This is a direct data-integrity and workflow-loss issue.

source_issues.title: Cline auto compacts context silently even with autocompacting setting disabled
source_issues.evidence: User disabled context compacting; context bar visibly runs backwards from 90k to 60k mid-task; agent forgets completed work and important instructions; no visual indicator of compaction occurring.

signals.topic: Settings panel inaccessible without account, blocking local-only provider (Ollama) configuration
signals.summary: Settings panel gear icon does nothing when user is not logged in, preventing configuration of local Ollama or other providers that don't require an account.
aliases: Gear icon unresponsive for non-account users
signals.review_reason: A core configuration UI element (settings panel) is completely inaccessible to users without an account. Users who want local-only setup cannot configure the extension, which is a primary use case. Blocks initial setup workflow.

source_issues.title: Settings panel does not work without an account
source_issues.evidence: User wants to use Cline with local Ollama only, no account; settings panel gear icon does nothing; workaround requires going through sign-up flow before settings become accessible.

signals.topic: Streaming HTTP requests hang indefinitely on network instability with no timeout, retry, or error surfacing
signals.summary: When TCP connections enter a half-open state (network drops), streaming LLM requests silently hang forever with no timeout, no error shown, and no retry triggered.
aliases: Streaming hangs forever on network drop

signals.topic: GitHub PR checks reuse stale task IDs on commit updates instead of creating fresh sessions
signals.summary: On pull_request.synchronize events, Continue re-posts original PR-open task IDs as commit statuses on new head commits instead of creating fresh check sessions. Stale check results persist for hours, causing misleading CI feedback and wasting developer time debugging non-existent issues.
aliases: Stale PR check results on updated PRs
PR check sessions not refreshed on new commits
CI feedback misleading due to stale check status
signals.review_reason: GitHub PR check feature produces persistently misleading CI feedback: stale check results from the original PR commit are re-posted as results on all subsequent commits. This directly wastes developer time (6 hours in reported case) and creates false CI failure signals. Multiple check files and commit events are affected. The root cause is clear: session keying omits head SHA.

source_issues.title: PR checks do not create fresh agent sessions on PR updates; stale task IDs re-post to new commits
source_issues.evidence: On PR #60 with 6 commits, same 3 task IDs reused across all commits. No new agent sessions created after PR-open. Stale failure persisted for ~6 hours. Developers pushed empty commits trying to trigger re-evaluation. Status looked like live check result but was actually old result. Suggested fix direction: session keying by (repo, PR number, head SHA, check content hash).

aliases: Hardcoded login shell flag breaks tcsh
Terminal tool unusable on tcsh/csh shells
signals.review_reason: Terminal tool is completely broken for all users with tcsh or csh as their default shell. Every command fails immediately with exit code 1. The root cause is a hardcoded -l flag incompatible with tcsh/csh. This blocks a core tool (terminal command execution) for an entire shell ecosystem.

source_issues.title: Terminal commands fail when `$SHELL` is set to `tcsh` due to hardcoded `-l` shell flag
source_issues.evidence: Linux + VSCode + Azure OpenAI. Every terminal command fails immediately with 'Unknown option: -l' and exit code 1. tcsh does not support the -l flag. All terminal commands blocked for tcsh users.

signals.topic: output_pydantic / response_model regression breaks tool execution on vLLM and OpenAI-compatible LLMs
signals.summary: Since v1.9.0, Task.output_pydantic is mapped to response_format and passed into the agent executor's tool-calling loop alongside tools. On vLLM and other OpenAI-compatible servers, the model receives both simultaneously and skips tool calls entirely, returning structured JSON directly instead — tools never execute.
aliases: response_format conflicts with tools on vLLM
output_pydantic causes tool-skipping on non-OpenAI LLMs
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed breaking regression introduced in v1.9.0 where output_pydantic conflicts with the tool-calling loop, causing tools to be silently skipped on vLLM and all OpenAI-compatible LLM backends. This directly blocks any crew using structured output with non-OpenAI models, which is a core user scenario. The bug is labeled bug, has a reproducible pattern, and affects a broad class of users (anyone using vLLM, Ollama, or other compatible backends).

source_issues.title: [BUG] `output_pydantic` / `response_model` leaks into agent tool-calling loop, causing tools to be skipped on non-OpenAI LLMs
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states: 'Since v1.9.0, Task.output_pydantic is mapped to response_model and passed into the agent executor's tool-calling loop. This causes the LLM to receive both tools and response_format simultaneously on every iteration. For LLMs served via vLLM (and likely other OpenAI-compatible servers), this results in the model skipping tool calls entirely and returning structured JSON directly — tools never execute.' Confirmed breaking change with a specific version tag.

signals.topic: OpenAI API key authentication fails with 401 inside CrewAI while working correctly outside
signals.summary: Users report that the same OpenAI API key that works in isolation (curl, Python script) fails with 401 invalid_api_key when executed inside CrewAI via crew.kickoff(). The root cause is not the API key itself but how CrewAI passes or configures it, blocking the primary execution flow.
aliases: API key 401 error only inside CrewAI
OpenAI auth fails in crew execution but not in direct API calls
signals.review_reason: This blocks the primary execution flow — users cannot run crews at all when using OpenAI as their LLM provider. The issue has a clear user scenario (API key works in curl/Python, fails in CrewAI), labeled as bug, and is currently open with no resolution. This is a critical authentication regression that makes CrewAI unusable for OpenAI users.

source_issues.title: [BUG] OpenAI API key works locally but fails inside CrewAI with 401 invalid_api_key
source_issues.evidence: Issue states: 'The same OpenAI API key works correctly when tested in isolation (Python script and curl), but fails when executed within CrewAI. Error code: 401 - Incorrect API key provided. The error only occurs during Crew execution (crew.kickoff).' The key is valid externally but fails inside CrewAI's execution path, indicating a credential-passing issue.

signals.topic: crewai package is uninstallable on Intel Macs due to LanceDB mandatory dependency dropping macOS x86_64 wheels
signals.summary: Since crewai 1.12.2, lancedb>=0.29.2 is declared as a mandatory core dependency. LanceDB dropped macOS x86_64 (Intel Mac) wheel builds at 0.29.2, causing pip to fail with ResolutionImpossible on all Intel Macs — even for projects that never use memory features.
aliases: Intel Mac installation failure from lancedb dependency
crewai uninstallable on x86_64 macOS due to missing LanceDB wheels

The dependency is declared mandatory in pyproject.toml, not optional. Currently open with no resolution, affecting a non-trivial user segment (all Intel Mac developers who cannot switch to ARM). Priority is P1 rather than P0 because the install failure is platform-specific rather than universally blocking.

source_issues.title: [BUG] crewai 1.12.2 uninstallable on Intel Macs: mandatory lancedb>=0.29.2 dependency has no macOS x86_64 wheels
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states: 'crewai 1.12.2 declares lancedb>=0.29.2 as a mandatory core dependency. lancedb dropped macOS x86_64 (Intel) wheel builds at 0.29.2, so crewai is uninstallable on all Intel Macs — even for projects that never use memory features.' Verified with uv pip install showing ResolutionImpossible.

signals.topic: create_crew() CLI --provider flag silently ignored due to loop variable shadowing
signals.summary: In cli/create_crew.py line 214, the for-loop uses 'provider' as its loop variable, which shadows the --provider CLI argument. After the loop, the provider variable holds the last key from ENV_VARS rather than the user's selection, causing the crew to be created with the wrong LLM provider silently.
aliases: CLI provider argument shadowing bug in create_crew
crewai create crew --provider flag silently ignored
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed code-level bug in the CLI entry point. When users run crewai create crew --provider openai, the provider argument is silently ignored and the last key from ENV_VARS is used instead. This causes incorrect crew configuration without any warning, affecting any user relying on the --provider flag. Though closed, the bug remains unfixed as the issue was closed without resolving the shadowing issue. Priority P1 because while it doesn't block installation, it silently misconfigures crews at creation time, which can lead to downstream failures or cost issues.

source_issues.title: [BUG] create_crew() loop variable shadows provider function parameter
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly shows the bug: 'In create_crew() (cli/create_crew.py), the for-loop on line 214 uses provider as its loop variable: for provider, env_keys in ENV_VARS.items(). This shadows the provider parameter that's passed in from the CLI (crewai create crew <name> --provider <value>). After the loop finishes, provider no longer holds the user's original selection.' The current parameter isn't used downstream, causing silent misconfiguration.

signals.topic: HITL pre-review with learn=True silently swallows all exceptions and bypasses human-feedback safeguards
signals.summary: When @human_feedback(..., learn=True) is used and lessons are recalled, _pre_review_with_lessons applies lessons via an LLM before presenting output for human feedback. Any exception in this path (network, auth, LLM error, structured-output issues) is caught silently and returns the original method_output, with no exception propagated, no warning logged, and no user notification — the human feedback safeguard is silently bypassed.
aliases: HITL fails open silently bypassing safeguards
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed bug in the human-in-the-loop safety mechanism. When any exception occurs during pre-review with learn=True, all exceptions are silently swallowed and the original output is returned without any warning or user notification — effectively bypassing the human feedback safeguard entirely. This defeats the purpose of HITL safeguards and can allow potentially harmful outputs to proceed without human review. The bug is labeled bug and has been confirmed. Priority P1 because while serious (safety bypass), the closed state and learn=True prerequisite limit immediate blast radius.

source_issues.title: [BUG] HITL pre-review fails open and silently bypasses automated safeguards
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly states: 'When @human_feedback(..., learn=True) is used and lessons are recalled, _pre_review_with_lessons attempts to apply those lessons via an LLM before presenting output for human feedback. If any exception occurs in this path (network or auth failure, LLM error, or structured-output issues), the implementation catches all exceptions and returns the original method_output. As a result: No exception is propagated, No warning or error is logged, The human feedback safeguard is silently bypassed.'

signals.topic: TransformersModel quantization_config parameter missing — GPU memory overflow when model should fit

signals.topic: MCP pre-flight HEAD request silently skips authenticated servers due to missing auth headers

source_issues.title: MCP pre-flight HEAD request missing authentication headers

All authenticated MCP servers fail pre-flight and are silently skipped, blocking users from using authenticated MCP integrations.

signals.topic: interrupt() in while loop causes duplicate resume value processing
signals.summary: When interrupt() is called inside a while loop (e.g., for human-in-the-loop input validation), previously supplied resume values are re-processed on every retry, causing unexpected duplicate execution of prior loop iterations instead of only processing the latest resume value.
aliases: interrupt() re-processes previous resume values in loop
signals.review_reason: Blocks the documented human-in-the-loop input validation pattern, a primary LangGraph use case. User reports following official docs verbatim and getting incorrect behavior. The scratchpad.resume mechanism incorrectly replays prior resume values when interrupt() is called inside a while loop.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Interrupt() in a loop will cause extra resumes

Root cause: scratchpad.resume ordered list does not account for re-entering the same loop body multiple times.

signals.topic: joinStream silently drops all subgraph events when stream_mode is specified on reconnect

Runs.Stream.join filter regression drops subgraph events
signals.review_reason: Breaks the core stream resumption pattern for production deployments using subgraphs. Subgraph events are silently dropped on reconnect when stream_mode is specified, making stream-based recovery unreliable across both Python and TypeScript SDKs.

source_issues.title: langgraph-runtime-inmem: Runs.Stream.join drops subgraph events when stream_mode is supplied (joinStream regression)
source_issues.evidence: Regression: initial stream returns 12 subgraph events but joinStream with stream_mode returns 0. Filter mismatch: write-side uses prefix matching, read-side uses exact string match. Breaks stream resumability for any subgraph workflow on both Python SDK and TypeScript SDK.

source_issues.evidence: 18 comments from affected users on LangGraph Cloud. Long-running tool calls (>180s) are silently re-executed on resume from checkpoint instead of resuming. Results in duplicate API calls, wasted LLM tokens, duplicate database writes, and inconsistent state with no user notification.

signals.topic: AIMessage type not msgpack serializable causing checkpoint failures
signals.summary: When graph state contains AIMessage objects (common in LLM-augmented graphs), checkpointing fails with 'TypeError: Type is not msgpack serializable: AIMessage'. Users must manually exclude messages from state as a workaround, degrading the core checkpointing developer experience.
aliases: checkpoint serialization fails with LLM output types
signals.review_reason: Checkpointing is a core persistence feature. When AIMessage objects appear in state (common in LLM-augmented graphs), checkpointing fails with TypeError. Users must manually exclude messages from state, degrading checkpointing developer experience. 22 comments confirm multiple users hitting this.

source_issues.title: TypeError: Type is not msgpack serializable: AIMessage
source_issues.evidence: 22 comments from users encountering TypeError when checkpointing graph state that contains AIMessage objects. msgpack cannot serialize AIMessage, causing checkpoint operations to fail. Users must manually exclude messages from state as a workaround.

signals.topic: psycopg OperationalError with SSL errors breaks Postgres checkpointing
signals.summary: Users encounter psycopg.OperationalError with SSL errors when using Postgres checkpointer. This intermittent failure prevents reliable state persistence and blocks production deployments that depend on Postgres checkpointing.
aliases: psycopg OperationalError SSL bad length in checkpoint
signals.review_reason: Postgres checkpointing is a key production persistence option. SSL OperationalErrors prevent reliable state persistence and directly block production deployments using Postgres. 48 comments indicate widespread and persistent issue across multiple versions.

source_issues.title: langgraph-checkpoint-postgres (psycopg.OperationalError: sending query and params failed: SSL error: bad length) encountered across multiple version
source_issues.evidence: 48 comments from users encountering psycopg OperationalError with SSL errors during Postgres checkpointing. Affects multiple versions and is intermittent. Blocks production use of Postgres checkpointer entirely.

signals.topic: Langfuse trace isolation failure causes cross-tenant data leakage in 1.14.1
signals.summary: After upgrading to 1.14.1, Dify spans were exported to wrong Langfuse projects belonging to other tenants. Sensitive trace inputs, outputs, metadata could be visible to other tenants. Caused by Langfuse v3 SDK attaching SpanProcessor to the global OpenTelemetry TracerProvider, so spans from all tenants export to the first configured tenant's project.
signals.review_reason: Cross-tenant data leakage is a critical security and privacy violation. Two users confirmed data leaked across tenants. Affects all self-hosted 1.14.1 deployments using Langfuse workflow tracing with multiple tenants. Confirmed by hotfix PR #36107.

source_issues.title: [URGENT] Langfuse trace isolation issue affecting users who installed 1.14.1
source_issues.evidence: Two users reported Dify spans appeared in wrong Langfuse projects. Sensitive trace data may have been exposed across tenants. Root cause: Langfuse v3 SDK uses global OpenTelemetry TracerProvider causing cross-tenant span leakage.

signals.topic: trigger_provider_refresh task storm causes 100% CPU on worker even with zero providers configured in 1.14.x
signals.summary: After upgrading to 1.14.0, the trigger_provider_refresh Celery task enters an infinite self-publishing loop on the trigger_refresh_publisher queue, causing 100% CPU usage and 10,000+ Redis writes per minute even when no model providers are configured at all.
signals.review_reason: 100% CPU storm on the worker is a severe resource exhaustion issue that renders the entire worker unusable. It occurs even with zero providers configured, meaning every self-hosted 1.14.0/1.14.1 deployment is affected. The task storm generates thousands of logs per minute and 10,000+ Redis writes per 60s, causing both CPU and I/O resource exhaustion.

source_issues.title: [Bug] 1.14.0 trigger_provider_refresh task storm causes 100% CPU on worker even with zero providers
source_issues.evidence: Task generates thousands of logs per minute, Redis saves 10,000+ changes every 60 seconds, worker CPU stays at 99-100%. Occurs even with zero providers configured. Root cause: task explicitly sets queue='trigger_refresh_publisher' and keeps getting re-published, creating an endless chain.

signals.topic: Password reset completely broken returning 400 invalid_or_expired_token in all 1.14.x versions
signals.summary: All password reset attempts fail with 400 invalid_or_expired_token in 1.14.0 and 1.14.1. Caused by a regression where the _TokenData TypedDict strips the 'phase' field that was added by a security fix, so the phase validation gate always fails. 100% of users attempting password reset are affected.
signals.review_reason: Complete auth flow breakage affecting 100% of users attempting password reset on 1.14.x. Users are permanently locked out of their accounts if they forget passwords since no admin bypass exists. The root cause is clearly identified as a regression from two interacting PRs in 1.14.0.

source_issues.title: Password reset always returns 400 invalid_or_expired_token in 1.14.x — _TokenData TypedDict strips the phase field
source_issues.evidence: 100% of password reset attempts fail. Root cause: #35425 added phase field to reset tokens, but #34380 refactored TokenManager.get_token_data to use Pydantic validation which silently strips the phase field from _TokenData TypedDict. The phase gate always fails, making password reset completely non-functional.

signals.topic: OpenAI-API-compatible LLM plugin credentials unavailable after upgrading to 1.14.1, models unusable and undeletable
signals.summary: After upgrading to 1.14.1, LLMs configured with the OpenAI-API-compatible plugin stop working. signals.review_reason: Blocks core model usage functionality for all OpenAI-API-compatible plugin users after upgrading to 1.14.1. Additionally, the delete action falsely reports success, causing data inconsistency. Both use and management of LLM configurations are blocked.

source_issues.title: OpenAI-API-compatible LLM plugin - credentials unavailable
source_issues.evidence: After update to 1.14.1, LLMs configured with OpenAI-API-compatible LLM plugin do not work. Model credentials unavailable. Unable to remove models - message says 'Action succeed' but model not deleted.

signals.topic: Iteration block fails with 'Working outside of application context' error when parallel mode is enabled
signals.summary: In Dify 1.14.1 cloud, enabling parallel mode on an iteration block causes the flow to fail with 'Working outside of application context' error. This blocks users from using the iteration block with parallel execution, a key workflow feature.
signals.review_reason: Blocks the iteration block workflow feature when parallel mode is enabled. This is a key workflow capability that becomes unusable in 1.14.1 cloud. The Flask application context error indicates a threading/async context isolation issue that prevents the iteration from running in parallel.

signals.topic: POST /configure endpoint missing role-based authorization — any API key holder can hijack global LLM/embedder configuration, exfiltrating all user memories and prompts
signals.summary: The /configure endpoint only checks token validity but never verifies the caller's role. Any holder of a distributed API key can redirect all LLM and embedder traffic to an attacker-controlled server, exfiltrating every user's prompts, memories, and embeddings. Config persists to DB, survives restarts, and affects all users globally. Full PoC confirmed 6/6 tests pass against a real Docker deployment.
aliases: Missing role check on global config endpoint
API key privilege escalation on configure endpoint
signals.review_reason: Critical authorization vulnerability with a confirmed PoC. Any API key holder (service/team member/CI pipeline) can silently redirect all LLM and embedder traffic to an attacker-controlled endpoint, exfiltrating all user prompts, memories, and embeddings. The attack is persistent (DB-persisted), affects all users globally, and requires only a distributed API key — a realistic and common deployment pattern. This is not a hypothetical: a full PoC with 6/6 passing tests is provided, demonstrating the complete attack chain from key compromise to data exfiltration.

source_issues.title: Missing Authorization on POST /configure Allows Any API Key Holder to Hijack Global LLM Configuration
source_issues.evidence: Full end-to-end PoC runs against a real Mem0 Docker deployment with AUTH_DISABLED=false. Registers admin, creates API key, uses ONLY the API key to redirect all LLM + embedder traffic to attacker endpoint. Captures user prompts, memories, embeddings. 6/6 tests pass. Config persists to PostgreSQL and survives restarts. Blast radius: global singleton affects ALL users, ALL API keys, ALL services on the instance.

signals.topic: @mem0/openclaw-mem0 npm package ships uncompiled TypeScript without dist/ — breaks OpenClaw gateway startup completely after plugin-validation tightening
signals.summary: The published npm package lacks compiled output, no main/module field in package.json, and no build script. Recent OpenClaw versions hard-require compiled ./dist/index.{js,mjs,cjs}. Installing the plugin prevents the gateway from starting at all with a non-obvious error. 'openclaw doctor --fix' does not fix it. Workaround requires manual TypeScript bundling, re-done on every reinstall.
aliases: OpenClaw plugin ships raw TypeScript source
Gateway fails to start after installing openclaw-mem0 plugin
signals.review_reason: Users installing the openclaw-mem0 plugin against current OpenClaw versions get a completely non-bootable gateway. This is a packaging/release defect: the published npm tarball does not contain compiled output. The failure is silent at install time but catastrophic at runtime — the gateway fails to start entirely. The recommended 'openclaw doctor --fix' does not resolve it, leaving users with no path forward unless they manually bundle TypeScript. Each reinstall re-introduces the problem, creating a recurring broken state.

source_issues.title: @mem0/openclaw-mem0: published package ships unbuilt TypeScript; bricks OpenClaw gateway after recent plugin-validation tightening
source_issues.evidence: OpenClaw gateway fails to start with error: 'Invalid config ... installed plugin package requires compiled runtime output'. Error does not clearly point to missing build. openclaw doctor --fix does not auto-build the plugin. Workaround requires manually running npx tsdown, must be re-run on every reinstall. Any user installing against a current OpenClaw gets a non-bootable gateway with no clear remediation.

signals.topic: Memory.add excludes metadata/app_id from Phase 1 retrieval and message partitioning — causes cross-context contamination in multi-app/multi-tenant deployments
signals.summary: Memory.add restricts search_filters to only user_id/agent_id/run_id, excluding metadata fields like app_id. The SQLite messages table is also scoped by those three keys only. The same user_id across different app_id values will share the recent message window and Phase 1 candidate pool. This is inconsistent with Memory.search which passes full filters dict including custom keys. Result is cross-context memory contamination in multi-app deployments.
aliases: app_id metadata not included in search filters
Phase 1 memory retrieval ignores metadata fields causing data leakage between apps
signals.review_reason: In multi-app/multi-tenant deployments, the same user_id across different app_id values share message windows and memory retrieval pools. This means app-a's memories can contaminate app-b's memory operations, and vice versa. The inconsistency between Memory.add (restricted filters) and Memory.search (full filters) creates silent data leakage between logically isolated application contexts. This is a correctness defect that breaks memory isolation — a core safety guarantee in multi-tenant setups.

source_issues.title: addMemory flow excludes metadata (e.g. app_id) from retrieval and message partitioning, causing cross-context contamination in multi-app setups
source_issues.evidence: Concrete reproduction scenario provided: same user_id with different app_id values share the message window and Phase 1 memory pool. app-b cannot add app-scoped facts because Phase 1 retrieval returns app-a's memories. Session scope excludes app_id, meaning the SQLite messages table for user-1 contains messages from both app-a and app-b without differentiation.

signals.topic: macOS Claude Desktop MCP configuration instructions are incorrect — npx mcp-add is rejected as invalid MCP server
signals.summary: The documented instructions for connecting mem0 MCP to Claude Desktop on macOS say to use 'npx mcp-add', but Claude Desktop rejects this as 'not a valid MCP server'. The correct method is under Settings -> Customise -> Connectors -> Add custom connector. Users following the docs cannot complete MCP setup on Claude Desktop.

npx mcp-add not valid for Claude Desktop integration

The documented 'npx mcp-add' approach is rejected by Claude Desktop itself, and the correct path (Settings -> Customise -> Connectors -> Add custom connector) is undocumented. This is a primary integration path that is entirely broken for macOS Claude Desktop users.

source_issues.title: [macOS] Incorrect instructions for Claude Desktop MCP configuration
source_issues.evidence: Claude Desktop explicitly rejects the 'npx mcp-add' approach as 'not a valid MCP server'. signals.topic: BM25 keyword search and entity extraction silently degrade to no-op for all non-English languages due to hardcoded English spaCy model
signals.summary: The v3 hybrid search pipeline hardcodes spaCy's English model (en_core_web_sm) for BM25 and entity extraction. For CJK, Arabic, Thai, Hindi, and other non-English scripts, BM25 becomes a silent no-op and entity boost disappears. Users see no error — search quality just silently degrades to semantic-only, missing precision improvements from exact-match on non-English employee IDs, names, and place names.
aliases: Hybrid search BM25 silently fails for non-English queries
Non-English users get degraded search quality without any error indication
signals.review_reason: The v3 hybrid search pipeline silently fails for all non-English queries — BM25 becomes a no-op and entity boost disappears with no error message. Users see no indication that the feature is degraded; search simply returns less accurate results. This affects the majority of global users (CJK, Arabic, Thai, Hindi, and other non-English deployments). The degradation is silent and invisible, making it particularly insidious. Users have no way to know their search results are suboptimal.

source_issues.title: BM25 keyword search and entity extraction are hardcoded to English
source_issues.evidence: For non-English deployments (Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Thai, Hindi, etc.), BM25 scores come back empty and entity boost disappears. No error is raised. Results are silently returned without the BM25 signal. Exact-match on non-English employee IDs, names, and place names does not work. This is the default experience for the majority of the global user base.

signals.topic: AG-UI streaming regression: MessageId deduplication causes tool events not rendered in frontend (two manifestations)
signals.summary: A regression in ChatResponseUpdateAGUIExtensions.cs (commit ca02146e) assigns a single fallback streamingMessageId to all events, causing ToolCallResultEvent to share the same MessageId as the assistant message. CopilotKit deduplicates by messageId, so tool result events collide with assistant messages and tool-call rows are not rendered. Additionally, AG-UI with multiple registered agents streams responses from all agents instead of just the target agent — same root cause (MessageId handling).
signals.review_reason: count=2 meets P0 threshold; both are main-flow blocking — AG-UI tool event rendering is completely broken for CopilotKit frontends after upgrading from 1.0.0 to 1.3.0, and multi-agent streaming incorrectly emits from all agents. Both are confirmed regressions with clear root cause (ca02146e). The user explicitly identifies this as a regression and provides a workaround (reverting to 1.0.0), demonstrating real production impact.

signals.topic: MCP credential leak: header_provider headers re-injected on cross-origin redirects via MCPStreamableHTTPTool._inject_headers
signals.summary: MCPStreamableHTTPTool unconditionally re-applies _mcp_call_headers ContextVar headers (including bearer tokens) on every outbound httpx request without origin checking. When httpx follows a cross-origin redirect and strips Authorization headers, the _inject_headers hook re-injects them to the attacker-controlled redirect target. This is a confirmed credential-leak vulnerability in the same class as CVE-2018-1000007 (curl), CVE-2024-37891 (urllib3). The first-party sample mcp_api_key_auth.py documents bearer token forwarding via this mechanism, making the leak path explicit.
signals.review_reason: P0 is justified despite count=1 because: (1) this is a critical security vulnerability (active credential leak) with a well-documented exploitation path and PoC; (2) the first-party sample explicitly demonstrates bearer token forwarding through this exact code path; (3) the bug is latent but becomes reachable as soon as the upstream mcp-sdk fix (modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk#2298) ships on PyPI, meaning the attack surface will widen soon; (4) the security keywords rule does not apply — this is not a generic 'security vulnerability' label, but a specific, reproducible credential-leak with clear user impact.

signals.topic: AgentSession state restore/resume fails: pending request not resumed after session persistence and deserialization
signals.summary: When a workflow pauses for human plan review (e.g., Magentic orchestration), the SSE stream emits a request_id. The user persists AgentSession state including pending request metadata, then restores the session and sends feedback for the same request_id. The session does not resume the pending request and errors instead. Affects any user attempting to persist/resume mid-workflow agent sessions.
aliases: session persistence pending request not restored
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is blocked — users cannot persist and resume agent sessions mid-workflow when waiting for human plan review. This is a session state restoration bug that prevents users from implementing a core use case (pausing/resuming multi-turn agent workflows). Confidence is high based on clear reproduction steps and explicit expected vs actual behavior.

signals.topic: .NET build failure: [MessageHandler] on partial Executor class fails with CS0534 (does not implement ConfigureProtocol)
signals.summary: When using Microsoft.Agents.AI.Workflows 1.5.0 with [MessageHandler] on a partial class inheriting from Executor, the build fails with CS0534 because ConfigureProtocol is not auto-generated. The user must manually implement ConfigureProtocol + ConfigureRoutes(AddHandler) as a workaround, defeating the purpose of source generation. Affects .NET developers using the workflows source-generation API.
aliases: MessageHandler partial Executor CS0534 build failure
signals.review_reason: Build failure blocking the primary development workflow for .NET developers adopting the [MessageHandler] source-generation API in version 1.5.0. The build error is a compile-time block — code cannot ship. While count=1, the impact is severe (complete build block) and the workaround is non-trivial (manual ConfigureProtocol implementation), making this a clear user pain point.

signals.topic: .NET AddWorkflow builder name mismatch: System.InvalidOperationException — workflow factory returned workflow with name '' instead of expected name
signals.summary: When calling builder.AddWorkflow('some-name', delegate), the builder validates that the workflow returned by the factory has the expected name, but AgentWorkflowBuilder.CreateHandoffBuilderWith() does not allow specifying a name and returns a workflow with empty name. This causes a System.InvalidOperationException at registration time. Affects .NET Aspire users wiring agents and workflows through DI.
aliases: workflow name empty string exception Aspire
signals.review_reason: Startup block — the DI registration of workflows in .NET Aspire fails at runtime with InvalidOperationException. The user explicitly notes this was 'already posted before in several issues, and seems to have been ignored after #1885 was marked Closed without being fully fixed', indicating a persistent unresolved problem across multiple releases.

signals.topic: GroupChat round-robin skips the last agent when max_round is an even number
signals.summary: When GroupChat is configured with max_round set to an even number (e.g., 4), the last agent (agent C in a 3-agent setup) is never selected in the speaker selection loop. This is caused by an off-by-one error in the round-robin implementation. The bug is reproducible in autogen-agentchat 0.4.x on Python 3.11 and was reported independently three times.
aliases: GroupChat speaker selection broken for even rounds
signals.review_reason: GroupChat is a core orchestration primitive. The round-robin bug causes a critical agent to be silently excluded from the workflow whenever max_round is even — a common configuration. The bug is non-obvious (agent appears to 'silently fail') and breaks the main orchestration flow. Three independent reports confirm it is reproducible and not an edge case. All three issues are closed, indicating the maintainers have acknowledged the bug.

source_issues.title: GroupChat round-robin skips agent when max_round is even
source_issues.evidence: With 3 agents and max_round=4, agent C never speaks. Off-by-one error in the speaker selection loop. Tested on autogen-agentchat 0.4.x on Python 3.11. State: closed.

signals.topic: AutoGen Studio WebSocket RCE — unauthenticated remote code execution via team_config
signals.summary: AutoGen Studio WebSocket endpoint accepts attacker-controlled team_config containing malicious FunctionTool with unsanitized source_code. FunctionTool._from_config() calls exec() on attacker-supplied Python code, achieving RCE with CVSS 9.8. Default AuthConfig sets type=none, requiring no authentication.
signals.review_reason: CVSS 9.8 unauthenticated RCE in default AutoGen Studio configuration — any user deploying AutoGen Studio with default settings is fully compromiseable via a three-step attack. This is a primary flow failure and critical security break with a public PoC.

source_issues.title: [Security] Critical: Unauthenticated RCE via WebSocket team_config (CVSS 9.8)
source_issues.evidence: Default AuthConfig type=none; FunctionTool._from_config() executes attacker-controlled source_code via exec() with no sanitization or sandbox. Full server compromise achievable with zero prerequisites and no user interaction.

signals.topic: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing, enabling host compromise via prompt injection
signals.summary: LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes it as a subprocess with full host privileges. Only a UserWarning is emitted at init time, which is easily suppressed in production pipelines. An agent processing untrusted data can be tricked into generating malicious code (e.g., credential exfiltration via subprocess), which is then executed with host-level access.
signals.review_reason: The executor is included in quickstart examples and ships as a default convenience option. The only safeguard is a suppressible warning, not a security control. Users following official quickstarts in production are exposed to full host compromise through any LLM processing untrusted content (web pages, user messages, documents). This is a primary flow security break with explicit attack scenario.

source_issues.title: [Security] LocalCommandLineCodeExecutor executes LLM-generated code without sandboxing
source_issues.evidence: Affected code in autogen_ext/code_executors/local/__init__.py lines 391-434 writes LLM-generated code to disk and executes via asyncio.create_subprocess_exec with no sandboxing. Only a UserWarning is emitted at construction — not a security control and easily suppressed. Attack: indirect prompt injection → malicious code written to disk → executed with host privileges → credential theft, lateral movement, data destruction.

signals.topic: Gemini models raise openai.BadRequestError when executing tool calls via AutoGen

signals.review_reason: Tool calling is a core feature of AutoGen agents. Gemini model users are blocked from using tool-calling workflows. While count=1, the bug is specific and reproducible, and the issue was acknowledged (closed after maintainer comment), indicating the bug is real. The failure blocks a primary use case (Gemini-powered agent with tools).

source_issues.evidence: Using Gemini 1.5 Pro with autogen-agentchat 0.4.1 and google-generativeai 0.8.0 — executing a tool call raises openai.BadRequestError. Issue closed after 1 comment. Specific to Gemini; other models work without this error.

UI mode global setup error swallowed

UI mode all tests fail silently 1.60 regression

signals.topic: Compound ANSI SGR color codes are silently dropped in HTML reporter and trace viewer
signals.summary: ANSI escape sequences using compound SGR codes (e.g., '\x1b[1;31m' for bold+red) are silently consumed in HTML report and trace viewer, rendering colored terminal output as plain text. Affects output from chalk, picocolors, vitest, jest, prettier, eslint, and all modern terminal-coloring libraries.
aliases: ANSI compound color codes broken in reporters
terminal color formatting lost in HTML report
signals.review_reason: Significant UX degradation in test reporting: compound ANSI color codes from standard tooling (vitest, jest, prettier, eslint, chalk, picocolors) are silently stripped, making HTML reports and trace viewers significantly harder to read. Root cause is identified and fix is straightforward, but user impact is widespread across all reporters.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Compound ANSI SGR codes lose styling in HTML reporter and trace viewer
source_issues.evidence: Root cause identified in ansi2html.ts line 30: `+codeStr` returns NaN for compound codes like '1;31', silently dropping all compound SGR sequences; affects HTML reporter, trace viewer, errorMessage, and codeMirror components; modern terminal-coloring libraries default to compound form

signals.topic: Deno runtime breaks when using request API with mTLS client certificates via SOCKS5 proxy
signals.summary: Using the Playwright request API in Deno with client certificates through a SOCKS5 proxy results in 'CertificateRequired' fatal alert and request failure, whereas the same setup works correctly in Node.js.
aliases: Deno request API mTLS over SOCKS5 broken
Deno playwright request client certificates proxy fail
signals.review_reason: Functional breakage of the request API in Deno runtime with a specific but realistic configuration (mTLS + SOCKS5 proxy). This is a runtime-environment-specific failure that prevents Deno users from performing API testing, a core use case of Playwright's request API.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Deno breaks when using `request` API
source_issues.evidence: Same mTLS client certificate + SOCKS5 proxy setup works in Node.js (returns 200) but fails in Deno with 'apiRequestContext.get: received fatal alert: CertificateRequired'; blocks users using Deno runtime from using critical request API features

signals.topic: WebKit on macOS returns Cocoa reference date epoch instead of DOMHighResTimeStamp for synthesized events
signals.summary: On macOS WebKit, Playwright-synthesized events return event.timeStamp values based on the Cocoa reference date (2001-01-01) instead of performance.timeOrigin, producing values ~8e11 instead of normal hundreds of milliseconds. Any code performing time-delta math on these timestamps produces wildly incorrect results.
aliases: synthesized event timestamp wrong on WebKit macOS
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption: WebKit on macOS returns wrong-epoch timestamps that silently produce incorrect results in any code treating event.timeStamp as DOMHighResTimeStamp. Values are well-formed numbers so errors don't throw — making this a particularly insidious bug that affects any event-timing or performance analysis logic.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: WebKit on macOS sets event.timeStamp to a value that looks like a Cocoa reference date
source_issues.evidence: event.timeStamp returns ~800152113482 ms (~25 years from 2001-01-01 Cocoa epoch) instead of values close to performance.now(); affects all Playwright input APIs (click, pointer, mouse events); real-user events and JS-dispatched events return correct values; regression since WebKit 18.2

signals.topic: .NET: JSON serializer options mismatch between tool schema and tool calls causes enum/int parameter deserialization to fail
signals.summary: KernelJsonSchemaBuilder uses JsonStringEnumConverter for tool schema generation, but KernelFunctionFromMethod.TryToDeserializeValue does not, causing System.ArgumentException and JsonException when enum or int parameters are used in any kernel function invocation.
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed bug reports with full stack traces and reproduction steps. This is a main-flow blocker: any user defining kernel functions with enum or int parameters will experience silent deserialization failures and ArgumentException crashes at runtime. Additionally, nullable enum schema generation produces invalid JSON schema that causes 100% tool call rejection in strict-mode LLMs. Count=2, both confirmed bugs with evidence.

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: JSON serializer options don't match between tool schema and tool calls, causing enum parameters to fail.
source_issues.evidence: Full stack traces showing System.ArgumentException (Object of type 'System.String' cannot be converted to type 'TaskReminder[]') and System.Text.Json.JsonException (JSON value could not be converted) when invoking kernel functions with enum parameters. signals.topic: exec_command yield_time_ms parameter silently capped at ~30s on initial command execution

Demonstrates inconsistent behavior between initial call and polling, disrupting agent orchestration of long-running terminal tasks (builds, tests, servers, migrations).
