signals.topic: Dangerous-command detection misses rm variants and sudo-wrapped rm
signals.summary: The dangerous-command heuristic for approval flows misses common rm patterns: plain rm with operands, split flags (-r -f), absolute path /bin/rm, and sudo-wrapped variants. Destructive commands may execute without approval prompts in filesystem protection workflows.
signals.review_reason: Safety mechanism gap with real impact: the dangerous-command detection used in approval flows fails to catch common rm variants. In filesystem-unrestricted or external approval configurations, destructive commands can bypass approval prompts entirely. Author provides a concrete proposed patch confirming this is a confirmed missing pattern.

source_issues.title: Dangerous-command detection misses plain rm and sudo-wrapped rm variants
source_issues.evidence: Heuristic only catches exact 'rm' + '-f' or '-rf' patterns. Misses: 'rm file.txt', 'rm -fr dir', 'rm -r -f dir', '/bin/rm -rf dir', 'sudo -n rm -rf dir'. When command is not classified as dangerous, the approval policy may silently allow it without surfacing a prompt — a confirmed safety gap in request-based approval flows.

signals.topic: Realtime known-tool failures (exception/timeout) do not send model-visible output, causing indefinite session hang
signals.summary: When a known function tool raises an exception (e.g. ToolTimeoutError with timeout_behavior='raise_exception'), no RealtimeModelSendToolOutput is sent back to the model. The model waits indefinitely until the server-side timeout (~30 seconds) fires, making the session appear to hang silently.
aliases: Realtime tool exception no model output
signals.review_reason: This is a clear main-flow blocker: the Realtime session hangs indefinitely because the model never receives a tool output notification when a known tool fails with an exception. The issue provides a full repro showing 'Model received tool output: False' and the model waits ~30 seconds. The bug is confirmed in the known-tool branch (line 697) while the same issue in the unknown-tool branch was already fixed by #3287.

source_issues.title: Realtime known tool failures (exception/timeout) do not send model-visible output
source_issues.evidence: Bug with full repro: known-tool branch at line 697 calls invoke_function_tool() without try/except. Exception propagates out, RealtimeError is emitted locally, but NO RealtimeModelSendToolOutput is sent back to the model. Model waits indefinitely for a function call result that never arrives (server-side timeout ~30 seconds). Session appears to hang. Related: #3286/#3287 fixed the same class of problem for unknown-tool branch.

signals.topic: AdvancedSQLiteSession.add_items() reports success after structure metadata failure — silent data loss
signals.summary: add_items() commits base message rows before writing message_structure metadata. If the structure write fails, add_items() returns without raising, making the save appear successful while messages are missing from get_items(). Retry logic cannot reliably determine whether to retry.
signals.review_reason: Three distinct SQLite session data-integrity bugs identified: (1) #3348 — add_items() returns success despite failing to persist metadata, causing silent data loss and broken retry logic; (2) #3361 — AsyncSQLiteSession lacks session_settings support, breaking API consistency with all other backends; (3) #3346 — delete_branch() leaves orphaned messages in the database, accumulating invisible rows. All three have full repros. Together they represent significant risk of data loss/inconsistency in production session persistence workflows.

source_issues.title: AdvancedSQLiteSession.add_items can report success after structure metadata failure
source_issues.evidence: Full repro with TypeError when AsyncSQLiteSession is given session_settings parameter, proving API inconsistency. add_items() logs error and returns without raising when metadata write fails, silently losing data.

source_issues.title: AsyncSQLiteSession does not support SessionSettings defaults
source_issues.evidence: AsyncSQLiteSession raises TypeError on session_settings parameter. Inconsistent with all other session backends (SQLiteSession, AdvancedSQLiteSession, Redis, Dapr, MongoDB, SQLAlchemy). Full repro shows: TypeError: AsyncSQLiteSession.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'session_settings'.

source_issues.title: AdvancedSQLiteSession.delete_branch() leaves branch-only messages in the base table
source_issues.evidence: Full repro shows delete_branch() removes turn_usage and message_structure rows but leaves agent_messages rows orphaned. After delete, branch-only messages remain in database but are invisible to get_items(). Causes database growth and audit noise.

signals.topic: AgentOutputSchema.name() crashes with AttributeError for Literal output types, blocking structured output agents
signals.summary: AgentOutputSchema.name() recursively assumes every typing argument has __name__, but Literal arguments are plain values (e.g. strings). This causes AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute '__name__' when formatting schema names for valid output types using Literal values.
signals.review_reason: Key structured output functionality (AgentOutputSchema.name()) crashes with a reproducible AttributeError for any output type containing Literal values. This blocks users from using common patterns like Literal['ok', 'done'] for validated string choice outputs. The crash occurs during agent trace initialization, preventing the agent from starting at all for affected output types. Full repro provided.

source_issues.title: AgentOutputSchema.name() fails for Literal output types
source_issues.evidence: Full repro: schema = AgentOutputSchema(cast(type[Any], Literal['ok'])); schema.json_schema() works but schema.name() raises AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute '__name__'. Nested forms like list[Literal['ok', 'done']] also fail. Pydantic models, plain dict, generic dict, and generic list work correctly — only Literal arguments cause the crash.

signals.topic: Nested handoff history flattening silently drops multiline and structured content, causing data loss in chained handoffs
signals.summary: When a nest_handoff_history summary is passed through another nested handoff, _extract_nested_history_transcript reconstructs the transcript by splitting on newlines and parsing 'role: content'. This loses: (a) content after the first newline, (b) structured content parts (lists) converted to plain strings.
signals.review_reason: Chained handoffs (a real production pattern) silently corrupt user message content: multiline text is truncated and structured content (e.g. multimodal input parts) is mangled into strings. This is data loss in the conversation history that reaches the next agent. The repro confirms content is permanently altered rather than just displayed incorrectly.

source_issues.title: Nested handoff history flattening drops multiline and structured content
source_issues.evidence: Full repro shows 'first line\nsecond line' content is truncated to 'first line' after second nested handoff pass. Structured content like [{'type': 'input_text', ...}, {'type': 'input_image', ...}] is converted to a JSON string. Both cases have complete repro scripts.

signals.topic: Local on_approval rejection reasons are dropped, model receives generic HITL message instead of custom reason
signals.summary: Local tool on_approval callbacks can return a rejection reason, but that reason is dropped before the rejection output is generated. The model-visible tool output falls back to the generic 'Tool execution was not approved' message instead of the callback's custom reason.
signals.review_reason: Custom rejection reasons from on_approval callbacks are silently dropped, causing the model to receive a generic 'Tool execution was not approved' message instead of the developer-specified reason. This degrades the agent's ability to understand why a tool was rejected, reducing the quality of agent responses during human-in-the-loop workflows. The issue affects all local tool types sharing the approval status helper.

source_issues.title: Local on_approval rejection reasons are dropped
source_issues.evidence: Full repro: on_approval callback returns {'approve': False, 'reason': 'Not allowed'} but model-visible output is 'Tool execution was not approved.' The callback's reason is silently dropped. Shell, apply_patch, and custom local tools all share the same approval status helper. Hosted MCP approval handling already propagates rejection reasons correctly.

signals.topic: Streaming tool_call fragments dropped when accumulate_delta receives duplicate index entries in first chunk, causing JSON parse failure
signals.summary: accumulate_delta() in _deltas.py (and identical code in _assistants.py) has two early-return branches that store the raw delta list on first chunk without merging by logical index. When a single SSE event contains two tool_call entries with the same index (e.g. name + arguments in one event), both entries are stored as separate list elements. Subsequent chunks merge into element [0] only, leaving the orphaned fragment in element [1]. The reconstructed tool_calls[0].function.arguments becomes invalid JSON that cannot be parsed. Confirmed broken on vLLM with speculative decoding enabled.
aliases: streaming tool_calls merge by position not index
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed bug reports (count=2) demonstrate the same root cause. Data loss in tool_call streaming produces unparseable JSON in a main user-facing path (tool use). Node SDK does not have this bug, confirming the issue is Python-SDK-specific. Both reports show concrete invalid-JSON output.

source_issues.title: `accumulate_delta` drops tool_call fragments when one chunk has multiple entries at the same `index`
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows accumulated arguments == ': "London"}' with '{"city"' stranded in orphan entry. Invalid JSON produced in production path. Issue is closed (fixed).

source_issues.title: Streaming tool_call deltas with duplicate indexes in first chunk are accumulated incorrectly
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced against vLLM with speculative decoding, a real-world production setup. Produces malformed tool_call JSON with stranded arguments.

signals.topic: Responses API multi-turn conversations 400 error on turn 2 when passing response.output back as input via model_dump()
signals.summary: Calling model_dump() on response.output items and passing them back as input to client.responses.create() causes a 400 error on turn 2 with 'Unknown parameter: input[1].status'. model_dump() fabricates 'status: None' and 'encrypted_content: None' fields for fields the API never returned. The API rejects null unknown parameters. Additionally, there is an undocumented pairing constraint requiring reasoning+message to be consecutive pairs. Root cause traced to openai/openai-openapi#536. Affects production services doing manual conversation history management. Downstream breakage confirmed in openclaw (64.9k forks), pydantic-ai, and openai-agents-python.
aliases: Responses API model_dump fabricates null fields causing 400 on turn 2
multi-turn conversation fails on second turn
signals.review_reason: Multi-turn conversation management is a fundamental use case. The bug makes model_dump() unsafe for conversation history reuse, breaking production services. Widespread downstream impact confirmed (openclaw, pydantic-ai, agents-python). Count=1 but high confidence with strong user impact evidence across multiple downstream projects.

signals.topic: Background Responses API failures do not map to typed exception classes, breaking retry logic
signals.summary: When Responses API runs with background=True and the run fails (status=failed or status=incomplete), the SDK returns HTTP 200 OK and surfaces the failure only in the response body as a free-form error.code string. The SDK's HTTP-status-code dispatcher never fires, so no typed exception (InternalServerError, RateLimitError, etc.) is raised. Callers cannot use isinstance checks for retry logic. The error.code values are undocumented, not stable, and do not map 1:1 to SDK exception classes. Incomplete runs use yet another vocabulary (incomplete_details.reason) with no mapping.
aliases: background run error.code not mapped to exceptions
retry logic broken for background responses API
signals.review_reason: Missing exception mapping for background Responses API failures breaks retry/backoff logic, which is critical for production reliability. While count=1, the impact is clear: retry on transient errors (rate limits, server errors) becomes impossible without this mapping, leading to silent failures and unnecessary user-visible errors.

source_issues.title: Background responses failures lack a stable code/name that maps to an exception class
source_issues.evidence: Feature request describing broken retry logic in production. Synchronous path has clean HTTP-status-code-to-exception mapping but background path has none. Any isinstance(e, RateLimitError) or isinstance(e, InternalServerError) check silently fails for background runs.

signals.review_reason: A defined role (publisher/admin) that is supposed to enable org publishing is completely non-functional for already-transferred skills. The slug management is also incorrect (stale personal namespace shown). This is a permission workflow bug that prevents org team members from publishing, not just an edge case.

source_issues.title: "ORG publisher/admin" user cannot publish skills in ORG
source_issues.evidence: User with publisher/admin role in baidu-maps org cannot publish skill after transfer. UI slug still shows username path instead of baidu-maps/mapv-three. Bug confirmed in browser website. Affects correct org namespace publishing.

signals.topic: Gateway onboarding wizard lacks Back navigation, trapping users at wrong step with no recovery path
signals.summary: The server-driven Gateway wizard has no Back/Previous button. Once a user advances past a step they cannot return. Combined with terminal-error input validation (e.g., entering an invalid URL on the API-key path), users are wedged at the wrong branch with no way to correct their input, effectively blocking onboarding completion.
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow blocking UX issue. Real user session evidence (Mike's session 2026-05-13) shows a user was permanently trapped at the wrong wizard step with no way to recover. The wizard Back button is absent from both the UI (src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Onboarding/Pages/WizardPage.cs:632-636) and the protocol. Not P0 only because count=1 in a single repo; severity is UX wedge rather than hard crash.

source_issues.title: Gap A: Gateway wizard has no per-step Back navigation (server-driven, needs wizard.previous RPC)
source_issues.evidence: Direct user evidence: Mike's 2026-05-13 session — picked the API-key option, ended up at custom-endpoint URL prompt, entered an invalid value, and had no way back to fix the choice. Root cause is architectural: the wizard is server-driven via wizard.start/wizard.next/wizard.status; wizard.back/wizard.previous RPC does not exist in the protocol surface (src/OpenClaw.Shared/OpenClawGatewayClient.cs:296). Users advancing past a step with bad input are permanently wedged.

signals.topic: Onboarding window silently disappears when setup is incomplete, leaving user with no UI after reaching the Ready screen
signals.summary: When the user completes the onboarding wizard at the Ready step but StartupSetupState.RequiresSetup still returns true (e.g., wizard never actually configured a provider), OnboardingWindow.OnWizardComplete silently does nothing. The window closes without opening the Hub window, and the user sees no UI — the tray icon remains but there is no visible hint anything is wrong, making the app appear crashed or frozen.
aliases: wizard complete silently closes window with no next UI
app disappears after onboarding ready step
signals.review_reason: This is a main-flow UX failure with direct user evidence. Mike's session log (2026-05-13) shows the exact code path firing: wizard reached Ready, OnboardingWindow silently closed without any follow-up UI, user was left with only the tray icon and no indication of what happened. The app visually disappears from the user's perspective, which is experienced as a crash/freeze. Code evidence confirms the unhandled branch at OnboardingWindow.cs:644-653.

source_issues.title: Wedge B: OnboardingWindow.OnWizardComplete silently closes window when setupStillRequired=true (Finish from Ready)
source_issues.evidence: Direct user evidence from Mike's 2026-05-13 session log: wizard reached Ready step, then OnWizardComplete logged 'skipping chat launch; route=Ready, setupStillRequired=True', the onboarding window closed, no Hub window opened. Source code at src/OpenClaw.Tray.WinUI/Onboarding/OnboardingWindow.cs:644-653 shows the unhandled branch: when finishedFromReady && setupStillRequired, nothing opens — the window simply disappears from the user's perspective.

signals.topic: Telegram channel integration failures — plugin auto-enabled but runtime fails, forum topic messages not processed, polling leases leak on restart
signals.summary: Telegram channel is broken in three distinct ways: (1) Windows AutoClaw: channel runtime never initializes despite plugin being auto-enabled, bot is unreachable; (2) Supergroup Forum Topics: inbound messages from forum topics are silently dropped — bot shows 'typing...' but no session is created and no response generated; (3) All platforms: Telegram polling leases leak across in-process gateway restarts, causing duplicate poller errors and potential silent message drops.
signals.review_reason: 关键集成功能不可用：Telegram是OpenClaw核心channel之一，但该channel在多个维度上出现故障。Windows平台channel runtime完全不启动（100%阻断）；Forum Topic消息被静默丢弃（bot在线但收不到消息）；polling lease跨进程重启泄漏导致855+错误/天且可能静默丢消息。三条独立证据覆盖Windows/Linux、多版本、受影响用户群广泛。

source_issues.title: Telegram plugin auto-enabled but channel runtime never starts on Windows AutoClaw 1.1.1.91 / OpenClaw 2026.3.11
source_issues.evidence: On Windows 11, plugin logged as auto-enabled but zero Telegram-related output — no getMe, no polling started, no errors. Bot unreachable on Telegram. 100% reproducible on this build.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: [5.10-beta.5] Telegram Supergroup Forum Topics — Inbound Messages Not Processed
source_issues.evidence: Bot shows 'typing...' on inbound forum topic messages but no session created and no response generated. Outbound to same topic works fine. Direct chat also works. Silent failure, no logs. Affects all supergroup forum topic configurations.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Telegram polling leases leak across in-process gateway restarts
source_issues.evidence: Stale polling lease entries persist across in-process restarts (Symbol.for Map never cleared on shutdown). Every bot account fails with 'duplicate poller' errors. 855+ errors logged over 5 hours across 5 agents. Potential for silent message drops when zombie pollers die and stale leases block new ones.

signals.topic: Empty response payloads=0 on all models blocks agent functionality on fresh install (v2026.5.7 regression)
signals.summary: Fresh install of v2026.5.7 returns empty responses with payloads=0 on every model and provider, making OpenClaw completely non-functional. Direct API tests confirm credentials are valid — the failure is entirely inside OpenClaw's response handling.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：v2026.5.7回归导致所有模型（haiku和sonnet）均返回空响应payloads=0，新装用户完全无法使用agent功能。直接curl验证API key有效，问题完全在OpenClaw内部响应处理流程。100%复现率，阻断新用户体验，是最严重的功能性回归。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Empty response payloads=0 on all models — fresh install
source_issues.evidence: Every message returns 'empty response detected... stopReason=stop payloads=0'. Affects both claude-haiku-4-5 and claude-sonnet-4-5 on fresh install. Direct API key verified valid via curl.

signals.topic: Thinking blocks in reasoning model conversation history cause HTTP 400 on GitHub Copilot provider, breaking all multi-turn conversations
signals.summary: When reasoning models generate <thinking> tags, they are stored in history and sent back on the second turn to GitHub Copilot, which rejects them with HTTP 400 — breaking every multi-turn conversation without exception.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：reasoning模型生成的<thinking>标签被存入conversation history后，在第二轮请求中被发往GitHub Copilot API时触发HTTP 400错误，导致所有多轮对话在第二条消息后彻底中断。无例外、100%复现，Copilot用户的多轮交互完全不可用。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Reasoning model thinking blocks (<thinking> tags) in conversation history cause HTTP 400 on GitHub Copilot provider
source_issues.evidence: Single-turn works. Every second message returns HTTP 400 from Copilot API. Payload inspection confirms {type: 'thinking'} block present in assistant message history array. Affects claude-sonnet-4.6 and claude-opus-4 via Copilot.

signals.topic: Dashboard bypasses login in Local auth mode (live) — authentication not enforced despite UI displaying auth mode
signals.summary: In Local auth mode set to 'live', the dashboard grants access without requiring any login credentials, even though the UI correctly displays 'Local auth mode (live)'. Users believe they are in an authenticated environment when they are not.
signals.review_reason: 认证被完全绕过：Local auth mode(live)下Dashboard无需任何凭证即可访问，用户以为处于认证保护状态实则公开暴露。报告者明确定义为安全漏洞。未授权用户可查看和操作所有Dashboard数据和功能。

source_issues.title: Dashboard bypasses login in Local auth mode (live)
source_issues.evidence: With Local auth mode set to 'live', dashboard is accessible without any credentials. UI shows 'Local auth mode (live)' but no login is required. Explicitly labeled as a security issue by reporter.

signals.topic: Tool execution failures are not retried — agent work stalls silently and sessions end normally without completing tasks
signals.summary: When a tool returns an error (e.g., ambiguous edit target), OpenClaw delivers the error but does not retry. The agent abandons the task and the session ends with stopReason=stop — no retry triggered, no error surfaced to user, work left incomplete.
signals.review_reason: 工作静默挂起：工具执行失败（如oldText歧义错误）时，OpenClaw将错误作为普通文本（isError=false）交付给模型，不触发重试机制。Agent收到错误后放弃当前任务，session正常结束（stopReason=stop）而用户毫无察觉。Telegram修复未持久化到MEMORY.md，工作成果丢失。

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Tool Execution Failure → No Retry → Work Stuck
source_issues.evidence: Agent attempted edit, got ambiguity error delivered as isError=false. Agent pivoted away, session ended with stopReason=stop. MEMORY.md never updated, Telegram fix not persisted. Framework tracks tool errors but doesn't act on them.

signals.topic: Long command-line argument values treated as file paths, causing OSError on startup
signals.summary: When --system-prompt-prefix or --custom-instruction contain very long values (e.g., detailed system prompts), aider misparses them as file paths, triggering OSError [Errno 63] 'File name too long' in pathlib.py at startup. This blocks users who rely on long custom instructions from using the tool.
aliases: OSError errno 63 command line args parsed as paths
signals.review_reason: This is a startup crash with count=2 (distinct issues with identical root cause) that completely prevents aider from launching for users with long custom instructions or system prompt prefixes. The crash occurs in main.py at the initial argument parsing stage (is_dir check), blocking the main use case of configuring aider behavior. High confidence due to identical stack traces across both reports.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 840
source_issues.evidence: OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long on macOS when --system-prompt-prefix with a long value is passed. Crash at main.py line 704 during Path(all_files[0]).is_dir() call, indicating the long argument value was incorrectly treated as a file path.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in pathlib.py line 840
source_issues.evidence: OSError: [Errno 63] File name too long on macOS when --custom-instruction with a long value is passed. Same root cause as #5126.

signals.topic: aiohttp module AttributeError causes startup crash on Windows
signals.summary: When importing litellm on Windows, aiohttp raises AttributeError: module aiohttp has no attribute ConnectionTimeoutError, causing aider to crash immediately at startup before any user interaction is possible.
signals.review_reason: This is a startup crash that completely blocks the main workflow on Windows. The AttributeError occurs during module initialization (litellm import chain), preventing aider from even starting. While count=1, the impact is severe — complete app unavailability — and it is a recent issue (2026-05-11).

source_issues.title: Uncaught AttributeError in __init__.py line 240
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: module aiohttp has no attribute ConnectionTimeoutError. Crash occurs during litellm import at startup on Windows 10, blocking the entire application from launching.

signals.topic: UnicodeEncodeError with surrogate characters causes uncaught exception on Windows
signals.summary: On Windows, when console output contains surrogate Unicode characters (e.g., from LLM-generated content), an uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in console.py line 2097 crashes the entire application mid-session, with no graceful error handling and an unhelpful 'PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8' hint that does not fix the issue.
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow runtime crash that occurs mid-session on Windows when LLM output contains surrogate Unicode characters. The exception propagates uncaught and crashes the entire application, blocking the user's active coding session. The PYTHONIOENCODING hint is a red herring for surrogate characters.

source_issues.title: Uncaught UnicodeEncodeError in console.py line 2097
source_issues.evidence: UnicodeEncodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't encode characters in position 2828-2829: surrogates not allowed. The error occurs during console output and propagates as an uncaught exception that crashes the running session. PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 is suggested but does not resolve the surrogate character issue.

signals.topic: Windows console stdout flush causes OSError mid-session
signals.summary: On Windows, during send output stream, sys.stdout.flush() raises OSError [Errno 22] Invalid argument, propagating through console.py and _win32_console.py, causing an uncaught exception that crashes the running session.
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow runtime crash that occurs mid-session on Windows during output stream handling. The crash propagates from stdout flush through console output code, crashing the active session. Combined with #5128 and #5129, Windows users face multiple crash scenarios, indicating a systemic platform compatibility issue.

source_issues.title: Uncaught OSError in _win32_console.py line 403
source_issues.evidence: OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument during sys.stdout.flush() and _win32_console.py write_text. Occurs mid-session in show_send_output_stream, causing uncaught exception that propagates and crashes the running application on Windows 11.

signals.topic: tree-sitter QueryError crashes repo map generation on Windows
signals.summary: On Windows with Python 3.12, the tree-sitter parser raises tree_sitter.QueryError: Invalid node type at row 2, column 2 in repomap.py get_tags_raw, causing aider to crash when attempting to generate a repo map — a core feature required for codebase-aware code editing.
aliases: tree-sitter QueryError Invalid node type repomap
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow runtime crash that blocks the repo map feature — a core functionality of aider for codebase-aware editing. The QueryError is uncaught and crashes the session. While count=1, it targets a key feature (repo map) used in the main coding loop.

source_issues.title: Uncaught QueryError in repomap.py line 302
source_issues.evidence: tree_sitter.QueryError: Invalid node type at row 2, column 2: module. Crash occurs in repomap.py get_tags_raw during repo map generation, which is a core aider feature. The error prevents the repo map from being built, blocking the main code-editing workflow on Windows.

signals.topic: undici v7 自定义 Agent 不解压 Content-Encoding 响应，导致 OpenAI 端点调用返回乱码并抛出 JSON 解析错误
signals.summary: promptfoo 在升级到 undici v7 后，getOrCreateAgent 创建的自定义 Agent 缺少 decompress 拦截器，导致压缩响应（gzip/Brotli）未被解压就直接被 text() 读取，后续 JSON.parse() 在原始字节上失败。所有使用 OpenAI responses API 或 chat completions 的 eval 均受影响，尤其是启用了 web_search 的场景。
aliases: JSON parse error on compressed API response
signals.review_reason: Issue #9214 明确描述了一个主流程阻断问题：undici v7 升级后，自定义 Agent 未安装 decompress 拦截器，导致压缩响应（gzip/Brotli）未被解压就流入 text() 和 JSON.parse()，所有使用 OpenAI 端点的 eval 均报 JSON 解析错误并失败。这不是边缘问题，而是核心 HTTP 调用链路的回归缺陷，影响任何通过 promptfoo 调用 OpenAI API 的用户场景（尤其是 web-search 场景下响应总是被压缩），且存在有效但需要用户手动配置的 workaround（per-provider Accept-Encoding: identity），说明影响面广。Issue 提供了完整根因分析、最小复现代码和环境信息，置信度很高，应标记为 P0。

source_issues.title: fetch() with custom undici Agent does not decompress Content-Encoding responses (Brotli/gzip → garbage)
source_issues.evidence: Issue 提供了最小复现代码和完整根因分析（undici v7 中 decompress 拦截器需要显式安装），影响 OpenAI responses API 和 chat completions 的所有调用，表现为 'Unexpected token <x>...is not valid JSON' 错误，阻断主流程。

signals.topic: Provider model incompatibility blocking real workloads and forcing user churn
signals.summary: Bedrock new models (openai-oss-120, qwen) not supported due to hardcoded settings; google-genai file upload gives cryptic error with vertexai config >20MB
signals.review_reason: Issue #21636 includes explicit user statement 'I have to move to langchain' demonstrating direct churn caused by Bedrock model incompatibility. Issue #21639 produces a cryptic upstream error for >20MB file uploads with vertexai config, blocking a legitimate use case without actionable feedback. Both represent concrete work-blockers in primary data ingestion and LLM call flows.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: google_genai produces cryptic errors for >20MB file uploads with vertexai config
source_issues.evidence: Uploading a file >20MB with vertexai config produces cryptic upstream error 'This method is only supported in the Gemini Developer client.' with no actionable guidance from llama-index. User is blocked from completing file upload workflow.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Bedrock Model Not Support - Qween, openai-oss-120
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly states 'I have to move to langchain. just leave the llamaindex for llm call.' — direct user churn evidence. Bedrock models openai.gpt-oss-120b-1:0 and qwen are hardcoded as unsupported.

signals.topic: Rate limiter and tool execution block asyncio event loop causing latency spikes and observability failures
signals.summary: TokenBucketRateLimiter/SlidingWindowRateLimiter async_acquire() uses threading.Lock blocking the event loop; FunctionTool sync fn does not propagate ContextVar breaking OpenTelemetry
signals.review_reason: Issue #21603 causes measurable latency spikes (up to 341ms blocks) and throughput collapse in async pipelines using rate limiters, directly impacting production reliability. Issue #21555 breaks OpenTelemetry distributed tracing for all non-async tool executions, which is a production observability blocker. Both are high-impact async runtime issues with reproducible evidence.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: async_acquire() in TokenBucketRateLimiter and SlidingWindowRateLimiter blocks the asyncio event loop
source_issues.evidence: TokenBucketRateLimiter.async_acquire() uses threading.Lock (a blocking OS syscall) inside an async method. Under high concurrency this freezes every other concurrent coroutine for the duration of the lock hold. Repro script shows event loop blocked 4+ times with max block of 0.341s. Latency spikes and throughput collapse in any async LLM/embedding pipeline using rate_limiter.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: ContextVar not propagated on non-async tool execution
source_issues.evidence: When using FunctionTool with fn (sync) instead of async_fn, ContextVars set by the calling context are not propagated into the tool. OpenTelemetry uses ContextVar to parent spans — all non-async tool calls produce orphan spans in traces. Users cannot own the ContextVar when it's owned by third-party packages like OpenTelemetry. This is a production observability breaking issue.

signals.topic: BM25 retriever silently returns wrong data due to IndexNode serialization mismatch
signals.summary: node.model_dump() replaced node.dict() breaking IndexNode.obj serialization/deserialization, causing BM25 to return incorrect node data on retrieval
signals.review_reason: Issue #21611 describes a silent data corruption bug in a core retrieval path. The BM25 retriever retrieves wrong data on retrieval without raising any error, meaning downstream applications act on incorrect information. This is a data integrity failure that cannot be detected by users.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: obj serialization mismatch
source_issues.evidence: node.dict() was replaced with node.model_dump() in PR #18447. node.dict() was subclassed to wrap IndexNode.obj with __type__ field, but model_dump() is not. Deserialization via metadata_dict_to_node() -> IndexNode.from_dict() -> json_to_doc() expects the __type__ wrapper and throws, silently replacing the obj with a backup TextNode. BM25 retriever retrieves wrong data on retrieval with no error raised — data corruption without any failure signal.

signals.topic: File handles leaked in HotpotQA evaluation benchmark causing descriptor exhaustion
signals.summary: Two unclosed file handles in hotpotqa.py: download function and run function never close files, risking descriptor exhaustion in repeated evaluations
signals.review_reason: Issue #21610 leaves file handles unclosed in the HotpotQA evaluation benchmark. File descriptor exhaustion causes hard process failures in long-running evaluation jobs. This is a resource leak that can crash benchmark workflows and is a well-documented Python best-practice violation.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: File handles not closed in HotpotQA evaluation benchmark
source_issues.evidence: Two file handles are never closed in hotpotqa.py: (1) save_file = open(...) for dev_distractor.json download without close or context manager; (2) f = open(dataset_path) for reading query_objects without closing. In long-running evaluation jobs this can exhaust OS file descriptors causing hard process failures.

signals.topic: AgentStream thinking_delta not populated for BedrockConverse thinking mode, forcing fragile workarounds
signals.summary: When BedrockConverse thinking is enabled, AgentStream events lack thinking_delta and delta fields during thinking phase, forcing manual raw dict inspection
signals.review_reason: Issue #20349 (triage-labelled bug) shows that thinking_delta is not populated on AgentStream events for BedrockConverse thinking mode, forcing users to implement a fragile workaround inspecting raw dicts. This breaks expected streaming behavior for agentic use cases and requires model-specific parsing logic. Though the issue is closed, the triage label and clear user impact evidence justify inclusion.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: thinking_delta not populated on AgentStream events when thinking is enabled
source_issues.evidence: When BedrockConverse thinking mode is enabled, AgentStream events during the thinking phase have event.delta = '' and event.thinking_delta = None. Users must manually inspect event.raw['delta']['reasoningContent']['text'] instead of using the documented event.thinking_delta field. This requires fragile, model-specific parsing that is not portable across LLM providers.

signals.topic: Memory search 完全失效 — 嵌入维度不匹配（768-dim vs 384-dim）

signals.topic: Hook 系统完全失效 — 模块路径不匹配导致所有钩子 MODULE_NOT_FOUND
signals.summary: ruflo init 写入的 hook 命令引用 ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/.claude/helpers/ 路径，但安装脚本将 helper 文件放在全局 ~/.claude/helpers/ 目录。结果：所有 Bash/Edit/Session 钩子在任何项目中触发 MODULE_NOT_FOUND，钩子系统完全不可用。
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但 review_reason 提供强用户影响证据：所有钩子在任何新项目（fresh install）中均触发 MODULE_NOT_FOUND，导致钩子功能完全不可用。这是安装脚本报错，属于主流程阻断。用户无论何时新建项目均会遇到。count=1 是硬约束，但该 issue 具备 P0 级别的用户影响，无需 count≥3 的支撑。

source_issues.title: [v3.7.0-alpha.27] Hook scaffolding writes $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR paths but installs helpers globally — every Bash hook MODULE_NOT_FOUND
source_issues.evidence: fresh ruflo init 后，所有 pre-bash、pre-edit、pre-session 钩子均报 MODULE_NOT_FOUND，hook 系统在任何新项目中完全不可用。这是一个安装脚本报错，直接阻断用户在任意新项目中使用钩子功能。

signals.topic: hooks_pretrain 提取 0 patterns — 非代码文件过多时遍历逻辑缺陷
signals.summary: hooks_pretrain 工具在深度优先遍历遇到超过 50 个非代码文件后才到达任何 .ts/.js/.py 文件时，报告 patternsExtracted: 0。该缺陷存在于 hooks-tools.js 的计数器逻辑中，导致文档密集型或规范密集型仓库无法提取任何模式。
aliases: hooks_pretrain extracts zero patterns for docs-heavy repos
pattern extraction fails on 50+ non-code files
signals.review_reason: 该 bug 存在明确复现场景（文档密集型仓库），导致核心功能完全失效。虽然 count=1，但缺陷明确，review_reason 清晰，属于已知根因的明确 bug，建议 P1。

source_issues.title: hooks_pretrain: extracts 0 patterns when first 50 files are non-code
source_issues.evidence: docs-heavy、specs-heavy、_bmad-output/ 等目录结构中，前 50+ 文件为非代码类型（.md/.json/.db/.yaml），hooks_pretrain 报告 patternsExtracted: 0，不输出任何模式。用户使用该工具对任何文档密集型项目时功能完全不可用。

signals.topic: Dashboard HTTP API routes use wildcard CORS allowing untrusted origin cross-site requests
signals.summary: Dashboard server exposes privileged /api/exec, /api/sessions, /api/kill and per-session /api/command with wildcard CORS (Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *). No origin/token/auth check. Malicious website can trigger CLI actions, start/end sessions as the local user.
signals.review_reason: 认证/权限缺陷：已验证恶意网站可通过 CORS 跨域调用 /api/exec 执行任意 CLI 命令、/api/command 驱动已认证会话。涉及本地权限控制平面，攻击者只需让用户访问恶意网页即可利用。虽然未观察到野外利用，但验证了攻击路径且影响已认证用户会话，属于高危安全缺陷。

source_issues.title: Dashboard privileged POST routes should reject cross-origin requests
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1345: Wildcard CORS on /api/exec (runs agent-browser binary with attacker-controlled args), /api/sessions, /api/kill. Validated dynamically: untrusted origin preflight accepted, POST to /api/exec executed successfully. No origin/token check.

source_issues.title: Per-session /api/command should require same-origin or token auth
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1344: Per-session POST /api/command relays JSON to daemon socket without origin check. If session stream port is discoverable, untrusted web content can drive authenticated browser sessions. Source/control/sink chain is explicit: wildcard CORS → no origin check → daemon socket write.

source_issues.title: Harden inspect-mode DevTools WebSocket handshakes
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1347: inspect mode WebSocket /ws path lacks capability token validation and non-local Origin check. Separate from dashboard hardening (#1346). CDP forwarding to unvalidated browser origins possible.

signals.topic: network route --body flag silently fails to stub HTTP responses
signals.summary: The --body flag on `agent-browser network route` has no effect because the CLI parser stores the body in a top-level JSON field but the daemon handler reads from a nested 'response' object. Intercepted requests pass through to real backend, completely breaking mock-based development workflows.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：--body mock 功能完全失效，导致基于 mock 的整个开发测试流程不可用。用户期望通过 --body 返回自定义响应，实际请求直接穿透到真实后端。对比 --abort 控制组确认底层拦截正常，说明是数据流断裂而非功能不可用场景。

source_issues.title: Bug: `network route --body` has no effect — CLI parser and handler field mismatch
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1353: The --body flag is completely non-functional. CLI parser stores body at top-level 'body' field, handler reads from nested 'response.body'. Result: RouteEntry.response is always None, requests fall through to real backend. Verified with control group showing --abort works correctly, proving the route matching logic itself is fine.

signals.topic: Proxy environment variables with trailing slash cause ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES on all platforms
signals.summary: When HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars contain a trailing slash (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:7890/), Chrome's --proxy-server argument rejects it, causing ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES on all URLs. Many system proxy GUIs automatically append trailing slashes.
aliases: proxy env var format breaks Chrome
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：所有通过代理访问 URL 的操作都会失败，错误为 ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES。触发条件极为常见（第三方代理工具自动添加 trailing slash），且无法通过用户配置绕过，因为根本原因在代码层未 trim。

source_issues.title: ERR_NO_SUPPORTED_PROXIES when proxy environment variables contain trailing slash
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1349: Confirmed reproduction on Linux/Kylin with Clash/V2Ray proxy. Chromium itself rejects --proxy-server=http://127.0.0.1:7890/ but accepts http://127.0.0.1:7890. Root cause is cli/src/native/cdp/chrome.rs directly passing proxy URL without trimming trailing slash. Many third-party tools (Clash Verge, Surge, GNOME/KDE Settings) automatically append trailing slash when constructing proxy URL.

signals.topic: Chrome crashes with 'trap int3' in Docker/容器 environment on every navigation
signals.summary: Chrome 147.0 (bundled) crashes with kernel 'trap int3' on every navigation attempt when running inside Docker containers. Process exits with SIGTRAP, making agent-browser completely unusable in containerized/CI environments.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：在 Docker/CI 环境中 Chrome 每次导航都会崩溃（trap int3），agent-browser 完全不可用。Docker 是现代 AI agent 和 CI 系统的标准运行环境，此问题影响所有容器化使用场景。

source_issues.title: Chrome 147.0 crashes with "trap int3" when running in docker
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1339: Chrome 147.0 bundled by agent-browser crashes on every navigation in Docker. Kernel logs show 'trap int3' SIGTRAP on chrome process. Reproduced on alpine/openclaw:2026.5.7 Docker image. Suspected root cause: --enable-unsafe-swiftshader flag incompatibility with containerized GPU/graphics stack. Blocks all Docker/CI agent workflows.

signals.topic: --headed mode fails to display browser window on Windows 11 when invoked from non-TTY context
signals.summary: On Windows 11, --headed mode does not surface any browser window when invoked from non-TTY contexts (PowerShell -File under bash 2>&1 redirection). Daemon claims headed mode but no window appears. Blocks all browser-mediated authentication flows (OIDC PKCE, manual login) in agent-driven scripts.
aliases: headed mode no window windows powershell non-tty
headed mode window visibility regression windows
signals.review_reason: 关键功能不可用：--headed 模式在 Windows 非 TTY 场景（agent 脚本的标配环境）下完全无法显示窗口，阻断所有需要人工参与的认证流程（OIDC PKCE、手动登录）。由于 agent 脚本的父 shell 本质上是非 TTY 的，这个问题实质上使 headed 模式在 Windows agent 场景下不可用。

source_issues.title: Windows 11: --headed not surfacing window when invoked from non-TTY context (PowerShell -File via bash 2>&1)
source_issues.evidence: Issue #1348: 5-attempt repro table shows headed mode works in real TTY pwsh but fails when stdout is redirected through bash 2>&1. Root cause suspected: Process.add_OutputDataReceived handler silently fails when stdout is piped (non-TTY). Blocks OIDC PKCE mint and manual login flows that require human interaction with live page. This is the exact workflow agent-browser is designed for on Windows.

signals.topic: Mistral provider silently drops stopSequences without warning, breaking stop-sequence functionality
signals.summary: The @ai-sdk/mistral provider receives the standard stopSequences parameter but emits an 'unsupported' warning and forwards nothing to the Mistral API, which natively supports stop sequences via its 'stop' param. Users get no indication that stop sequences are silently ignored.
signals.review_reason: Feature works incorrectly in a critical path (stop sequence truncation). Silent failure means users cannot rely on finishReason for Mistral, leading to unexpected full-length responses with no error signal.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/mistral: stopSequences silently dropped instead of forwarded as Mistral's native `stop` param
source_issues.evidence: stopSequences parameter silently dropped with unsupported warning. Mistral API natively supports stop sequences but adapter does not forward them. finishReason never becomes 'stop'.

signals.topic: Amazon Bedrock sends empty assistant content blocks for step-start boundaries, causing 400 API errors
signals.summary: When convertToModelMessages splits a UI message at step-start boundaries where a step contains only provider-invisible content (e.g., empty text), Bedrock skips the content but still sends an assistant message with content: [], which Bedrock rejects as an invalid empty message.
signals.review_reason: Main flow (multi-step AI conversations) fails with a hard API error. Step-start blocks are a standard SDK feature; users hitting this will see complete request failures with no workaround besides patching locally.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock sends empty assistant content for UIMessage step-start blocks
source_issues.evidence: Bedrock API returns: 'The content field in the Message object at messages.N is empty. Add a ContentBlock object to the content field'. Request fails at API level with 400.

signals.topic: tool.toModelOutput providerOptions silently dropped, Anthropic cache_control never reaches the API
signals.summary: tool.toModelOutput accepts a providerOptions field that is never propagated to the tool-result message part. For Anthropic, this means cacheControl set inside toModelOutput never reaches the API, silently preventing prompt caching for tool-result content with zero user indication.
aliases: anthropic cache_control silently ignored in tool results
signals.review_reason: Direct financial impact: prompt caching is a cost-reduction mechanism. Silent failure means users pay full price for repeated tool-result content without knowing caching is not applied.

source_issues.title: `tool.toModelOutput` returned `providerOptions` silently dropped, Anthropic `cache_control` never reaches the API
source_issues.evidence: providerOptions.anthropic.cacheControl set in toModelOutput never reaches the API. cache_creation_input_tokens stays at 0 with no warning. User has no signal that caching is not engaged.

signals.topic: Amazon Bedrock throws for image-url/file-url in tool-result content instead of auto-downloading (inconsistent with user-message behavior)
signals.summary: Bedrock auto-downloads URL-sourced images in user messages but throws AI_UnsupportedFunctionalityError for the same URL type inside tool-result content, creating an asymmetric and surprising failure that blocks multi-turn tool-use workflows with Bedrock.
signals.review_reason: Tool-use workflows in Bedrock break when the tool returns an image URL, which is a legitimate and common pattern. The inconsistency (works in user messages, fails in tool results) creates unpredictable failures.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/amazon-bedrock: image-url in tool-result throws instead of auto-downloading
source_issues.evidence: Throws AI_UnsupportedFunctionalityError: 'unsupported tool content part type: image-url'. Same URL pattern works in user-message content. No documented workaround.

signals.topic: File attachments over 32MB fail with opaque error on Azure OpenAI
signals.summary: When sending file attachments over 32MB via Azure OpenAI using the SDK, requests fail with a 'failed to download file' error. The exact limit is undocumented in the SDK, leaving users confused about which file sizes are supported.
signals.review_reason: File upload is a core use case. The opaque error message and undocumented limit cause user confusion and production failures. Users need clear documentation or a better error message.

source_issues.title: Failed to upload files urls can not be larger than 32 mb
source_issues.evidence: User reports file uploads above 32MB fail with 'failed to download file' error on Azure OpenAI (gpt-5.4-mini). No documentation in SDK about this limit.

signals.topic: Server Actions FormData regression: file input mismatch and empty FormData after 16.2.6 upgrade
signals.summary: Forms using useActionState + server action receive corrupted or empty FormData in 16.2.5/16.2.6. File input forms produce mismatched FormData on resubmit; non-file forms receive empty {}. Caused by CVE-2026-23870 DoS fix in react-server-dom-turbopack. Both regressions break core form submission flow entirely.
aliases: useActionState file input FormData mismatch on resubmit
Server Actions receive empty FormData after 16.2.6 security upgrade
FormData corruption in Server Actions regression
signals.review_reason: Two confirmed regressions in 16.2.5/16.2.6 blocking core form submission via Server Actions. #93822: file input FormData mismatch on resubmit; #93754: empty FormData {} after 16.2.6 security upgrade. Both directly break the primary use case of server actions (form handling), affecting any user upgrading from 16.2.4.

source_issues.title: useActionState with form containing file input receives missmatched FormData
source_issues.evidence: First form submit: FormData matches. Resubmit: only 'attachments' field reaches server, all other fields lost. Broken in 16.2.5/16.2.6/16.3.0-canary.12+. Works in 16.2.4.

source_issues.title: Server Actions receive empty FormData after upgrading to 16.2.6 (security release regression)
source_issues.evidence: Forms using useActionState + server action receive empty FormData {} server-side after upgrading to 16.2.6. All form inputs present in DOM at submission time. Caused by CVE-2026-23870 DoS fix in react-server-dom-turbopack. Not present in 16.2.2 or canary.

signals.topic: Turbopack production build chunk filenames with multiple dots trigger WAF 403
signals.summary: Turbopack generates chunk filenames with 3+ dots (e.g., 0od.e4.nsryo4.js) which web application firewalls interpret as 'multiple file extension' attack patterns and block with HTTP 403. Webpack-based builds are unaffected. Production deployments behind WAFs fail entirely.
aliases: Turbopack chunk filenames cause WAF false positives
Turbopack 3+ dots in chunk names blocked by WAF
signals.review_reason: Turbopack production builds are completely broken when deployed behind any WAF that implements 'multiple file extension' detection. Chunks with 3+ dots are blocked with 403, preventing the app from loading. Affects all Turbopack production users behind WAFs — a major production deployment blocker.

source_issues.title: Turbopack production build generates chunk filenames with multiple dots that trigger WAF 403 responses
source_issues.evidence: Turbopack generates chunk filenames like '0od.e4.nsryo4.js' with 3+ dots. WAFs interpret this as 'multiple file extension' attack pattern and block with 403. Chunks with 1-2 dots return 200 OK. Webpack builds generate WAF-friendly names. Production deployment behind WAF fails completely.

source_issues.title: Turbopack production build generates chunk filenames with multiple dots that trigger WAF 403 responses
source_issues.evidence: Duplicate of #93790. Closed as invalid link but same core issue.

signals.topic: updateTag does not invalidate prefetched RSC payloads after Server Actions
signals.summary: After calling updateTag() following a Server Action, navigation back to a previously visited route renders stale prefetched RSC payloads instead of fresh data. Users see outdated content (e.g., 0 comments) until a hard refresh. Affects both standard prefetched Links and Cache Components.
aliases: updateTag not invalidating prefetched RSC when navigating back
stale RSC data shown after Server Action due to updateTag
signals.review_reason: Users see stale content after Server Actions with updateTag due to cached RSC payloads not being invalidated. Two confirmed reports showing same pattern across different config states. Impact is data staleness rather than complete failure.

source_issues.title: updateTag does not invalidate prefetched RSC payloads when returning via prefetched Link
source_issues.evidence: After updateTag('items') following a Server Action, navigation back to / renders stale prefetched list payload. Row shows '0 comments' until hard refresh. With prefetch={false} or on 16.2.6 (in reduced repro) it works correctly.

source_issues.title: updateTag does not invalidate prefetched RSC payloads with Cache Components
source_issues.evidence: With cacheComponents: true, calling updateTag('items') after Server Action does not invalidate already-prefetched RSC payloads. Back navigation renders stale data until manual refresh.

signals.topic: Pages Router Turbopack route loader times out before page registration
signals.summary: pageLoader.loadPage() rejects with 'Route did not complete loading' despite all static chunks returning HTTP 200 and being fully downloaded. routeLoader.onEntrypoint is never called, so routes never register. Blocks page loading in Pages Router with Turbopack + i18n locale-prefixed URLs + assetPrefix + deploymentId.
aliases: Pages Router route never registers with Turbopack
pageLoader timeout despite successful chunks Pages Router
signals.review_reason: Page loading is blocked for Pages Router users using Turbopack with i18n locale-prefixed URLs. Chunks load successfully but the route never registers, causing pages to fail to display. Complex interaction of 5 flags/options means many real-world deployments are affected.

source_issues.title: Pages Router Turbopack route loader times out before page registration despite successful chunks
source_issues.evidence: pageLoader.loadPage() rejects with 'Route did not complete loading' even though route chunk loader was invoked and all static chunk requests returned 200. Route never registers through window.__NEXT_P.push and routeLoader.onEntrypoint is never called. Affects Pages Router + Turbopack + i18n locale-prefixed URLs + assetPrefix + deploymentId + separate static asset origin.

signals.topic: next/image: 0-byte cache file permanently poisons disk-LRU cache, breaking all image optimization
signals.summary: A single 0-byte file left in .next/cache/images/ (e.g., from Ctrl-C kill mid-write on Windows) causes 'LRUCache: calculateSize returned 0' error that permanently poisons the disk-LRU singleton. Every future image optimization request fails for the entire application lifecycle until cache deletion.
aliases: next/image LRU cache poisoning from 0-byte file
image optimization permanently broken after 0-byte cache entry
signals.review_reason: A single 0-byte file (extremely easy to produce via Ctrl-C) permanently breaks the entire next/image optimization system for the app until manual cache deletion. Critical image rendering feature is permanently disabled. Easy to reproduce and common in Windows dev environments.

source_issues.title: next/image: a single 0-byte file in .next/cache/images/ permanently poisons the disk-LRU singleton
source_issues.evidence: A 0-byte file in .next/cache/images/ (left by Ctrl-C kill mid-write on Windows) causes 'LRUCache: calculateSize returned 0' error that permanently poisons the disk-LRU singleton. Every future image optimization request fails. Suggested fixes: skip 0-byte entries during init, atomic writes, or don't poison the singleton on error.

signals.topic: Process group race condition: Turbo signals task complete before subprocess writes declared outputs, causing dependent tasks to fail in CI
signals.summary: When a task's subprocess leaves the tracked process group (via detached:true, setsid, or setpgid) before writing declared outputs, Turbo prematurely signals task completion and schedules dependents. On Linux CI this fails ~1.2% of the time; synthetic tests show 99-100% failure rate. Affected tasks fail with 'Could not resolve' / 'Cannot find module'.
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：CI 构建中任务完成信号竞争导致下游任务随机失败。真实 CI 环境中 1.2% 失败率，synthetic 测试高达 99-100%。关键功能（remote cache + output hashing + dependent scheduling）核心路径受影响，用户被迫修改工具链或接受不可靠构建。

source_issues.title: Task signaled complete before subprocess writes declared outputs when descendants leave the tracked process group
source_issues.evidence: On Linux CI ~1.2% failure rate for real-world bunx --bun <cli> toolchains; synthetic tests show 99.5-100% failure rate with detached/double-fork/delay-pgid modes. Dependent tasks fail with 'Could not resolve' errors because outputs not on disk. Fix PR #12790 exists but covers only in-group case; intentional-escape modes are follow-up.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker with literal workspaces + bun install fails: 'Workspace not found' errors in pruned output
signals.summary: When turbo prune --docker is used with a package.json that contains literal workspace paths (not globs) alongside bun, the pruned output cannot be installed in out/full because workspace entries are missing.
signals.review_reason: 影响 Docker 容器化构建主流程：prune --docker 是 monorepo 部署到容器的核心功能，当与 bun 生态的 literal workspaces 组合时完全失效。关键功能不可用，用户无法完成 Docker 构建工作流。

source_issues.title: literal workspaces + `turbo prune --docker` + `bun install` fails
source_issues.evidence: Running `bun x turbo prune --docker app` followed by `cd out/full && bun install` fails with 'error: Workspace not found' for all literal workspace entries. Works correctly with glob-based workspaces. Also needs compatibility with bun catalogs feature.

signals.topic: schema.json for v2-9-12 returns 404, breaking turbo.json codemod and update commands
signals.summary: The schema file for turbo version 2.9.12 is not deployed to the expected URL, causing pnpm dlx @turbo/codemod@latest update to write an invalid schema URL into turbo.json.
signals.review_reason: 升级流程阻断：用户运行 codemod update 命令后会得到无效的 turbo.json schema URL，导致后续 turbo 命令行为异常。影响所有通过 codemod 升级到 2.9.12 的用户。

source_issues.title: schema.json for v2-9-12 is not deployed (404)
source_issues.evidence: https://v2-9-12.turborepo.dev/schema.json returns 404. Running `pnpm dlx @turbo/codemod@latest update` writes the broken URL into turbo.json. Users upgrading to 2.9.12 end up with invalid config.

signals.topic: turbo affected fails to resolve base branch 'main' in GitHub Actions CI, causing all packages to be treated as changed
signals.summary: In GitHub Actions, turbo cannot resolve the 'main' branch because only 'origin/main' exists in the shallow clone. This causes the 'affected' command to fall back to 'assuming all files changed', completely bypassing incremental builds in CI.
signals.review_reason: CI 增量构建核心功能完全失效：affected 命令是 monorepo CI 优化的基石。GitHub Actions shallow clone 场景下无法解析 main 分支，导致所有包被标记为 affected，完全绕过了 turbo 的增量执行优化。影响所有在 GitHub Actions 中使用 affected 的用户。

source_issues.title: `affected` failing to resolve main branch in GitHub action
source_issues.evidence: GitHub Actions shallow clones don't have 'main' ref locally, only 'origin/main'. turbo affected fails with 'ambiguous argument main' and falls back to 'assuming all files have changed'. All packages are treated as affected, destroying the CI optimization purpose. Workaround is to manually `git branch main origin/main` in the workflow.

signals.topic: SIGINT not forwarded to subprocess when script-shell=sh, preventing graceful shutdown on Windows
signals.summary: When running turbo on Windows with script-shell=sh (the default for many Node tools), pressing Ctrl+C does not forward SIGINT to the subprocess, so graceful shutdown handlers never fire. Works correctly with script-shell=bash.
signals.review_reason: Windows 用户关键功能不可用：graceful shutdown 是长时间运行服务（dev server、watch mode）的核心需求。使用 sh 作为 script-shell 时（Windows npm 默认行为）无法优雅终止进程，可能导致数据丢失、端口占用等后果。用户明确指出这是 Windows 平台的阻断问题。

source_issues.title: `SIGINT` is not forwarded properly when `script-shell=sh`
source_issues.evidence: With script-shell=sh, Ctrl+C causes immediate process exit without triggering graceful shutdown handlers in the subprocess. With script-shell=bash, the graceful shutdown sequence fires correctly. Windows users who cannot use bash (security policy restrictions) are blocked from graceful shutdown.

signals.topic: Services-mode + middleware.ts causes silent deploy failure at 'Deploying outputs' stage
signals.summary: When a Next.js project uses experimentalServices (services-mode) with at least one non-root service, presence of middleware.ts causes every deploy to fail at the 'Deploying outputs' stage with a generic error message and no actionable diagnostics. The root cause is that scopeRouteSourceToOwnership rewrites middleware route `src` regex with ownership guards but does not exempt middleware routes (only `handle` routes are exempted), corrupting the route metadata and triggering a silent crash during output finalization.
aliases: Deploying outputs silent crash with middleware
signals.review_reason: Deploys fail silently with generic error, blocking the main deployment flow. Root cause is identified and deterministic. Community threads confirm broader impact. Users must either remove middleware.ts or abandon services-mode — both are significant workflow disruptions. Count=1 is below P0 threshold, so P1 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: Services-Mode: Middleware routes are not exempted from scopeRoutesToServiceOwnership, breaking deploy outputs
source_issues.evidence: Deterministic failure with minimal 5-file sandbox. Removing middleware.ts → deploy succeeds. Re-adding → fails again. Also correlates with broader community incident from 2026-05-07. Internal support cases referenced (01kpgVUAoxBA9kuW, 01161162).

signals.topic: vercel env add reports success but silently stores empty string for environment variable values
signals.summary: The `vercel env add` CLI command (v53.3.2) reports 'Added Environment Variable' with a success message, but the actual stored value is an empty string. This happens across all input patterns (stdin, --value flag, file redirect). The silent failure means users do not know their env vars were not set until later when application behavior breaks.
aliases: vercel env add empty string silent failure
CLI env variable set reports success but stores empty
vercel env pull returns empty despite CLI success
signals.review_reason: High-severity silent failure: CLI reports success but the env var is stored as empty string. This directly causes production outages when secrets are silently zeroed (Stripe webhooks, HMAC keys, service tokens). Users have no error signal. 100% reproducible. Count=1 but severity warrants P0 due to explicit evidence of production secret management impact.

source_issues.title: vercel env add reports success but stores empty string (CLI 53.3.2)
source_issues.evidence: 100% reproducible across all three input patterns (stdin, --value flag, file redirect). grep on pulled .env shows empty string. Dashboard env-var add works correctly — CLI-only regression. Security impact: secret rotation (Stripe keys, HMAC keys, service tokens) silently zeroes out values with a green CLI receipt.

signals.topic: vercel logs pagination returns duplicate entries when result set exceeds 50 records and --limit > 50
signals.summary: The `vercel logs --json --limit N` command with N > 50 returns duplicate entries once the result set crosses the 50-record page boundary. The server-side logs endpoint ignores the page parameter and returns the first page repeatedly, causing the CLI to accumulate duplicate records until --limit is reached. Users observability and debugging workflows are degraded.
aliases: logs command returns same records repeatedly
log pagination server-side ignores page parameter
signals.review_reason: Pagination bug causes data integrity issue for a core observability command. Reproducible, impacts anyone needing to view >50 log entries. Not a deployment blocker but degrades debugging workflows. Count=1 and only CLI affected, so P2.

source_issues.title: vercel logs returns duplicate entries when there are more than 50 results and --limit > 50
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows: --since 7min (28 logs) → 28 unique. --since 10min (100 limit) → 50 unique repeated twice. Duplicates are byte-identical. User identifies server-side as root cause: /api/logs/?page=N ignores page param while reporting hasMore:true.

signals.topic: AI/ACP features fail across multiple providers — crashes, authentication errors, and API errors
signals.summary: Three distinct ACP-related failures: (1) Codex CLI crashes mid-session leaving chat unusable after restart; (2) Codex CLI authentication with ChatGPT returns 'Resource not found'; (3) DeepSeek API returns reasoning_content error when tool calling is enabled. All three affect core AI workflow in Zed, leaving users unable to use AI assistance reliably.
signals.review_reason: Three related ACP integration failures across Codex and DeepSeek providers. Each blocks AI-assisted coding workflow. Count=3 meets frequency threshold for consolidation. Different failure modes but same root system (ACP).

source_issues.title: Codex CLI crashes 'Server exited with status exit status: 1 Error: ACP error: Internal error: "failed to send response, receiver dropped"'
source_issues.evidence: Codex CLI crashes mid-session with ACP internal error. Chat disappears and is gone after Zed restart. Platform: macOS 26.3, Zed 1.1.8.

source_issues.title: Zed editor codex-cli returns error 'Resource not found' during Reauthentication using Login with ChatGPT
source_issues.evidence: After installing codex-cli from ACP registry, 'Login with ChatGPT' returns 'Resource not found' error. AI authentication completely broken.

source_issues.title: Error with deepseek-v4-pro tool calling via OPEN CODE API KEY
source_issues.evidence: When using DeepSeek with thinking mode and tool calling enabled, API returns 'reasoning_content in thinking mode must be passed back to the API'. ACP-level API integration error breaks the feature.

signals.topic: Terminal SSH error on Flatpak and resize glitch on Windows — terminal reliability issues
signals.summary: Two terminal issues: (1) Zed Flatpak on Linux produces libselinux.so.1 version error when opening terminal via SSH connection — confusing warning messages appear; (2) On Windows, resizing terminal and navigating to previous command causes command to display in wrong position, making terminal unusable after resize.
signals.review_reason: Two terminal reliability issues across platforms. Both make terminal harder to use in specific workflows. The Flatpak libselinux warning is a known compatibility issue; the Windows resize glitch actively breaks the terminal UI after resize. count=2, each affects different platforms but same feature (terminal).

source_issues.title: Terminal Error when SSH into VM from Flatpak
source_issues.evidence: Flatpak-installed Zed produces libselinux.so.1 error on terminal open via SSH. Error message appears but terminal 'works fine' after — however the error is confusing and may indicate deeper compatibility issues.

source_issues.title: terminal's previous command (key up, down) glitch
source_issues.evidence: On Windows 10 with Zed v1.1.8, resizing terminal and pressing up arrow shows previous command in wrong position. Terminal display becomes unreliable after resize.

signals.topic: Editor crashes on startup on Linux with Intel Arc GPU and Vulkan driver (wgpu device lost)
signals.summary: Zed 1.1.x crashes immediately on startup on Linux systems with Intel Arc B580 GPU using xe kernel driver and Mesa anv drivers. The crash occurs after the first frame is rendered, with a wgpu panic 'Parent device is lost'. Users must use software renderer workaround (VK_ICD_FILENAMES) to run the editor at all.
signals.review_reason: Complete editor startup failure on specific GPU/hardware combination. Users cannot launch Zed at all without workaround. Kernel-level GPU hang confirmed in dmesg logs. Clear reproduction path and workaround exist. Severity: blocks main workflow entirely.

source_issues.title: Crash on startup on Linux with Intel Arc and Vulkan
source_issues.evidence: Editor crashes before window appears on Intel Arc B580 GPU with xe kernel driver. wgpu panic: 'Parent device is lost'. Software renderer workaround (llvmpipe) works. Kernel logs show GPU engine reset and timeout.

signals.topic: Agent overwrites entire files instead of applying targeted edits — blocks code review workflow
signals.summary: When the AI agent edits existing files, it sometimes rewrites the entire file instead of applying targeted diffs. The file shows all-new green code with no diff highlighting, no red deletions shown, and no per-line accept/reject. Users cannot compare changes with the original code.
signals.review_reason: Core code review workflow is broken — users cannot see what the agent changed, only the full new content. Forces binary accept/reject instead of line-by-line review. Clearly a significant UX regression in AI-assisted coding.

source_issues.title: agent overwrites files instead of edit them for comparison
source_issues.evidence: Agent rewrites entire file showing all code in green (no diff). Red deletions not displayed (marked '-0'). User forced to accept or reject on per-file basis, not per-line. 'Incredibly annoying and frustrating'. Previously this worked correctly.

signals.topic: Remote connection fails with client-ready timeout — blocks remote development workflow
signals.summary: Connecting to a remote macOS server via Zed Remote results in 'client did not become ready within the timeout' error. Users cannot use Zed for remote development at all on macOS remote setups.
signals.review_reason: Remote development — a key Zed selling point — is completely broken for this configuration. Blocks the entire remote workflow with a clear timeout error.

source_issues.title: Remote Connect: client did not become ready within the timeout
source_issues.evidence: Remote connection to macOS Server fails with 'client did not become ready within the timeout'. Remote development workflow completely blocked.
